summary: Main conjectures for modular forms and their families, Part II: all-prime CM zeta-element main conjectures. The roadmap starts where ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L0 (the cohomological formulation) stops and proves, for every CM newform of weight k ≥ 2 and every prime p including 2, Kato's rational main conjecture ξ(H²(V)) = ξ(H¹(V)/Z(f)) (Burungale–Tian Theorem 2.6). Its arithmetic input is the equivariant main conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields over Z_p[[Gal(K(p^∞f)/K)]][1/p] in corrected form, with the Euler factors at the primes of f prime to p that Burungale–Tian's Theorem 2.1 omits, proved from Johnson-Leung–Kings' all-prime main conjecture at regular height-one primes. CZ.0–CZ.1 are the early foundations shared with the Burungale–Kobayashi–Ota designs: the CM ray tower and its unit and class modules, Kato's CM theta function, standard elliptic units, the Kronecker limit formula, the elliptic-unit module, Kato's CM realization and his elliptic-unit reciprocity law (Prop. 15.9). CZ.2–CZ.3 are the integral layer (the elliptic-unit Euler system, Johnson-Leung–Kings Theorem 5.2, Rubin's Theorem 4.1, and at split primes the Coleman/Katz form and the anticyclotomic θ-components used by Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner). CZ.4 is the rational equivariant equality. CZ.5 carries the CM descent of Kato §15 (comparison map, Lemma 15.13 and its contained-field variant 15.14, the CM case of Kato Theorem 12.4 and Prop. 15.17). CZ.6 proves the equality step Kato §15 lacks (via Lemma 14.15), the bridge (15.16.1), Theorem 2.6, and exports the normalization dictionary to CMRankZeroConverse. Independent review corrected the statements and interfaces, but the exact Coleman-map/image assertions and ray-tower closure remain unverified; this is a partial plan requiring revision.

nodes.title: The CM ray-class tower and its two-variable Iwasawa algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field with a fixed embedding K ⊂ C, p a prime and f a nonzero ideal of O_K. Put K(p^∞f) = ∪_n K(p^n f) ⊂ K^ab (K(a) the ray class field of modulus a) and G = G_{p∞f} = Gal(K(p^∞f)/K) with its profinite topology. For a complete discrete valuation ring O finite flat over Z_p (in applications O = O_λ), the Iwasawa algebra is R_O = O[[G]] = lim_{K'} O[Gal(K'/K)], over finite K ⊂ K' ⊂ K(p^∞f), and R = Z_p[[G]]. The group G is the product of its finite torsion subgroup Δ = Δ_f and a subgroup Γ ≅ Z_p², the latter mapping isomorphically onto Gal(K_∞/K) for the unique Z_p²-extension K_∞ of K; a splitting G ≅ Γ × Δ is chosen and is part of the data. Hence R_O ≅ O[Δ][[S,T]] noncanonically: a three-dimensional semilocal ring, a finite product of local rings. When O contains the values of the characters of Δ, the normalization of R_O in its total quotient ring Q(R_O) is ∏_{χ∈Δ^} O[[Γ]](χ), and R_O[1/p] equals its normalization with p inverted. A height-one prime q of R_O is regular if p ∉ q and singular if p ∈ q. For a finitely generated R_O[1/p]-module M that is torsion (killed by a non-zero-divisor), ξ(M) denotes the invertible ideal ∏_q q^{length(M_q)} of R_O[1/p], the product over the height-one primes q, all of which are regular after inverting p.
hypotheses: K is imaginary quadratic; f is any nonzero ideal; p is any prime, p = 2 and p = 3 included.
No hypothesis p ∤ #Δ_f is made; when p divides #Δ_f the ring R_O is neither a domain nor normal.
The splitting G ≅ Γ × Δ is chosen; statements that depend on it say so.
proofSteps: Import the inverse limit of ray class groups with p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus, and its dimension formula, from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0: for K imaginary quadratic the unit rank is zero, so there is no Leopoldt defect and the Z_p-rank of G is r₂ + 1 = 2.
Identify G with that limit through the global Artin map for the actual ray class fields of ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, using the ray class carriers of GlobalNumberFields Layer 2.
The torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian pro-finite group of this shape is finite and has a complement isomorphic to Z_p²; choose one, compatibly with the restriction G → Gal(K_∞/K).

Use the existing completed group algebra and its map/projection API (ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 prerequisites; current Tau Ceti completedGroupAlgebra and completedGroupAlgebra.map), specialized to the arithmetic group G; a choice of topological generators of Γ gives O[Δ][[S,T]].

Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 7.2: O[Δ] ⊂ ∏_χ O with cokernel killed by #Δ, so after tensoring with O[[Γ]] the inclusion into ∏_χ O[[Γ]](χ) is an isomorphism after inverting p, and the product is normal. Lemma 7.6 then identifies localizations at regular primes.
Characteristic ideals of torsion R_O[1/p]-modules are defined componentwise on the normal ring ∏_χ O[[Γ]](χ)[1/p], where PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4's height-one length formalism applies.
acceptance: For K = Q(i), p = 2 and f = (1), Δ is trivial and G ≅ Z_2²: Z_2[i]^× = μ_4 × (a group ≅ Z_2²) and the global units μ_4 are the whole torsion.
For K = Q(i), p = 5 and f = (1), Δ ≅ Z/4, of order prime to 5; for K = Q(i), p = 2 and f = (3), Δ ≅ Z/8 and p divides #Δ.
The restriction to K(μ_{p^∞}) maps G onto Gal(K(μ_{p^∞})/K), which is the full cyclotomic group G_∞ exactly when K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}).

nodes.title: Iwasawa cohomology of the ray tower with general coefficients
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated Z_p-module (or O-module) T with continuous Gal(K̄/K)-action, unramified outside a finite set, put H^q_{p∞f}(T) = lim_{K'} H^q_ét(O_{K'}[1/p], j_*T), the limit over finite K ⊂ K' ⊂ K(p^∞f) along corestriction, where j is the inclusion of the open subscheme over which T is lisse (Kato's convention 8.2: the generic-point direct image, not extension by zero and not unrestricted cohomology of a larger S). The corresponding continuous Galois-cochain construction uses T ⊗ R_O^ι. Identifying it with these j_* groups requires the inertia and coefficient-limit comparisons recorded below; no unrestricted derived j_*/Rj_* equivalence is asserted. Each H^q_{p∞f}(T) is a finitely generated R_O-module, zero for q ∉ {1, 2} (Kato 15.6), Perfectness is asserted only in the cases of Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.3: RΓ(O_K[1/p], Λ(η)(1)) for their finite-order character η, and RΓ(O_K[1/pf], Ω(1)); it is not asserted for arbitrary T over a nonregular Ω. The variant H^q(O_K[1/pf], R(1)) of Johnson-Leung–Kings (13) replaces O_{K'}[1/p] by O_{K'}[1/pf]. A continuous character χ: G → O^× gives the semilinear twist isomorphism H^q_{p∞f}(T) ≅ H^q_{p∞f}(T(χ)) as follows: with the natural left deck action, φ_χ(x) = x ⊗ t_χ satisfies φ_χ(rx) = Tw_{χ^{-1}}(r)φ_χ(x), where Tw_χ(g) = χ(g)g. The inverse is semilinear for Tw_χ; the basis t_χ is fixed as part of the twisting data.
hypotheses: T is a finitely generated Z_p- or O-module with continuous action, unramified outside a finite set of places of K.

The j_* étale definition is retained. Any identification with continuous cochains must include the non-p inertia and coefficient-limit hypotheses; Selmer L3 currently supplies only a degree-one comparison in its stated cyclotomic setting.
K has no real place, so the 2-cohomological dimension of O_{K'}[1/p] is two and p = 2 needs no real-place correction.
proofSteps: Use the general inverse-corestriction construction of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3/iwasawa-cohomology and its continuous-cochain Shapiro theorem; the quotient is the CM ray group, not only a procyclic group.

Selmer L3/etale-iwasawa-comparison supplies a degree-one unramified comparison in cyclotomic towers subject to coefficient-limit hypotheses. Extend it to this ray tower with explicit inertia terms before identifying the j_* complexes. This is a recorded supplier gap, not a formal consequence of Shapiro.

Finite generation and vanishing outside degrees 1 and 2 are the claims of Kato 15.6 for this totally complex tower. Perfectness is used only with the exact coefficients and open schemes of Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.3; arbitrary finitely generated coefficients over Ω are not covered.

For the perfect complexes in the preceding step, use the derived coefficient and subgroup base-change statements of Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.4. Applying them to general ramified j_* complexes still needs the preceding comparison gap.
Fix a basis of the character line. Natural deck action gives g(x ⊗ t_χ) = χ(g)(gx ⊗ t_χ), hence φ_χ(gx) = χ(g)^{-1}gφ_χ(x). This fixes the inverse in the semilinearity convention.
acceptance: H^0_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) = 0 (Johnson-Leung–Kings (14)).
Over the base K = Q in place of an imaginary quadratic field, the same definition with the cyclotomic tower is Kato's H^q(T) of 8.2, so the two constructions agree where both apply.

nodes.title: The tower unit module h¹ and class module h²
nodes.statement: With the notation of the ray tower, h¹ = lim_{K'} (O_{K'}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p) and h² = lim_{K'} Cl(K')(p), the limits over finite K ⊂ K' ⊂ K(p^∞f) along the norm maps, where Cl(K')(p) is the p-primary part of the ideal class group of K'; G acts through its quotients Gal(K'/K), making both R-modules. In Johnson-Leung–Kings' notation h¹ = E′_∞ and h² = A_∞, and E_∞ = lim (O^×_{K(p^n f)} ⊗ Z_p) ⊂ E′_∞ is the module of global units.
hypotheses: The limits run over all finite subextensions, equivalently over the cofinal family K(p^n f), n ≥ 1.
Norm maps on S-units and on class groups are the field norm and the norm of ideals, respectively.
proofSteps: Form the inverse systems of finitely generated compact Z_p-modules O_{K'}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p and Cl(K')(p) with norms; their limits are compact R-modules (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2 for the general construction of arithmetic inverse limits).
The class group carrier is Mathlib's ClassGroup of O_{K'}; its p-primary part is the p-Sylow subgroup.
Compare with Johnson-Leung–Kings §5.4: E′_∞, E_∞ and A_∞ are the same limits indexed by K(p^n f).
acceptance: The definition presupposes nothing about class numbers of the layers.

proofSteps: At a finite layer: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0/s-unit-kummer-identification gives H^1(G_{K',S}, Z_p(1)) ≅ Z_p ⊗ O_{K',S}^× for S the places above p and ∞; the j_* convention at primes away from p does not change H^1 with Z_p(1) coefficients since units are unramified away from p.
The identifications commute with corestriction versus norm (same node).

Take the inverse limit of the compatible finite-level Kummer isomorphisms. Functoriality of inverse limits preserves isomorphisms; no assertion that all inverse limits are exact is needed for this step.

nodes.title: Class groups and H² of the ray tower agree in codimension one
nodes.statement: There is a homomorphism of R-modules h² → H^2_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) whose kernel and cokernel are finitely generated Z_p-modules; in particular (h²)_q ≅ H^2_{p∞f}(Z_p(1))_q for every height-one prime q of R (Kato (15.6.2)). At each finite layer it comes from the Kummer sequence: 0 → Pic(O_{K'}[1/p])(p) → H^2(O_{K'}[1/p], Z_p(1)) → lim_n Br(O_{K'}[1/p])[p^n] → 0, the last term being the kernel of the sum map Z_p^Σ → Z_p on the set Σ of places of K' above p, and Cl(K')(p) → Pic(O_{K'}[1/p])(p) is onto with kernel generated by the classes of the primes in Σ.
hypotheses: The number of places of K(p^∞f) above p is finite (each prime above p is finitely decomposed in the Z_p²-direction and Δ is finite).
proofSteps: Take cohomology of the Kummer sequence of G_m on O_{K'}[1/p]: Pic gives the first term and the p-power torsion of the Brauer group the last.

Identify the Brauer group of O_{K'}[1/p] through the global Brauer sequence (ClassFieldTheory Layer 10): its p-power torsion is the kernel of the sum of local invariants at the places above p (no real places).
Compare Cl(K′) and Pic(O_{K'}[1/p]): the quotient by the classes of the primes above p.

Pass to the limit over the tower. The Brauer terms and the classes of primes above p are bounded by the finitely many places above p in K(p^∞f), so they contribute finitely generated Z_p-modules, which are pseudo-null for R (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4/pseudo-null) and vanish at every height-one prime.
Retain both correction terms through the limit, as the brief requires; only after localization at height one do they disappear.
acceptance: When every prime above p is totally ramified in K(p^∞f)/K, the correction terms have Z_p-rank at most the number of primes above p in K.

nodes.title: Euler-factor comparison of H² over O_K[1/p] and O_K[1/pf]
nodes.statement: Write H^i_S = lim_{K'} H^i(O_{K'}[S^{-1}], Z_p(1)) over finite K ⊂ K' ⊂ K(p^∞f). Then H^1_p = H^1_{pf}, and restriction gives an exact sequence of R-modules 0 → H^2_p → H^2_{pf} → ⊕_{𝔩|f, 𝔩∤p} Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]] → 0, where D_𝔩 is the decomposition group of 𝔩 in G, of Z_p-rank one. Each Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]] is torsion but not pseudo-null; after inverting p it is killed by 1 − Frob_𝔩^{-1} on the components where 𝔩 is unramified, and its localization vanishes at every height-one prime of R[1/p] lying on a component on which the inertia group I_𝔩 ⊂ G acts nontrivially.
hypotheses: 𝔩 runs over the prime ideals of O_K dividing f and not dividing p.
Frob_𝔩 denotes the Frobenius of 𝔩 in G/I_𝔩, which has infinite order because 𝔩 is finitely decomposed in K_∞/K.
proofSteps: At each finite layer K′ the localization triangle for Spec O_{K'}[1/pf] ⊂ Spec O_{K'}[1/p] and purity (cohomology with supports at a place w | 𝔩 of K′ is RΓ(κ(w), Z_p)[−2] for Z_p(1) coefficients; Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.3 proof) give the exact sequence 0 → H^1(O_{K'}[1/p]) → H^1(O_{K'}[1/pf]) → ⊕_{w|𝔩} Z_p → H^2(O_{K'}[1/p]) → H^2(O_{K'}[1/pf]) → ⊕_{w|𝔩} H^1(κ(w), Z_p) → 0, the first map being the valuations at w.

Pass to the limit along corestriction. On the degree-two supported terms H^0(κ(w), Z_p) = Z_p corestriction is multiplication by the residue degree, which grows without bound because Frob_𝔩 has infinite order in G/I_𝔩; their limit is zero, so H^1_p = H^1_{pf}.

On the degree-three terms H^1(κ(w), Z_p) ≅ Z_p corestriction is the identity summed over the places above, so the limit of ⊕_{w|𝔩} Z_p is the compact module Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]]. Limits of compact modules are exact, giving the short exact sequence.
D_𝔩 has Z_p-rank one (𝔩 is unramified in K_∞ and finitely decomposed there), so Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]] is torsion of codimension one, not pseudo-null.

Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.3 computes the determinant of the supported complex as (1 − η(𝔩)Frob_𝔩^{-1})^{-1} on η-components unramified at 𝔩 and as the unit ideal on ramified components; after inverting p this is the vanishing statement at height-one primes on which I_𝔩 acts nontrivially.
acceptance: On the trivial-character component the factor 1 − Frob_𝔩^{-1} is a non-unit of R[1/p] for each 𝔩 | f with 𝔩 ∤ p, so H^2_{pf} and H^2_p have different characteristic ideals whenever f has such a prime factor.
If every prime factor of f lies above p the sequence reduces to H^2_p = H^2_{pf}.

nodes.title: Finite generation and torsion of the class module (weak Leopoldt for the ray tower)
nodes.statement: h² and H^2_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) are finitely generated torsion R-modules: each is killed by a non-zero-divisor of R. The proof given here goes through weak Leopoldt for the ray tower, H^2(G_{K(p^∞f),S}, Q_p/Z_p) = 0 for S the places above p; the sources state only the torsion assertion.
hypotheses: Any prime p, any nonzero f.
proofSteps: Weak Leopoldt for cyclotomic towers: for every number field F, H^2 of the Galois group of the maximal extension of F(μ_{p^∞}) unramified outside p with Q_p/Z_p coefficients vanishes (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.2, Iwasawa's theorem).

K(p^∞f) is the union of the fields K′(μ_{p^∞}) for finite K ⊂ K′ ⊂ K(p^∞f), since K(μ_{p^∞}) ⊂ K(p^∞). Cohomology commutes with this direct limit, so the H^2 with Q_p/Z_p coefficients vanishes for the ray tower.

Poitou–Tate duality in the limit (ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7/derived-global-duality) turns this into: H^2_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) has R-rank zero, i.e. is torsion, given finite generation from ray-tower-iwasawa-cohomology.
Transfer to h² through class-module-h2-comparison: the kernel and cokernel are finitely generated over Z_p, hence torsion over R.
acceptance: The module H^2_{pf} is also torsion (h2-euler-comparison adds torsion terms).

nodes.title: Finite generation, torsion-freeness and generic rank of the unit module
nodes.statement: h¹ is a finitely generated torsion-free R-module (no nonzero element is killed by a non-zero-divisor of R), and for every height-zero prime q of R the localization h¹_q has dimension one over the field R_q.
hypotheses: Any prime p, any nonzero f; R_q is a field for q of height zero.
proofSteps: Finite generation follows from tower-kummer-identification and the finite-generation statement of Kato 15.6, without invoking arbitrary-coefficient perfectness.

The rank-one assertion is Kato 15.6. To close its proof from the suppliers, prove the global Euler-rank formula for the totally complex Z_p² ray tower, including p = 2 and the finite Δ-components, and combine it with tower-class-module-torsion. Selmer L3/iwasawa-finiteness-euler currently states the rank formula only for odd-p cyclotomic towers.

Torsion-freeness is also asserted in Kato 15.6. Vanishing of the norm limit of roots of unity controls Z_p-torsion only; it does not identify all R-torsion. A CM ray-tower version of the Iwasawa H¹ torsion lemma is still required. The former perfectness/roots-of-unity argument is withdrawn and the missing lemma is recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Logarithm and logarithmic derivatives of the theta function as Eisenstein–Kronecker series
nodes.statement: For Im τ > 0 and z ∉ Zτ + Z, E(k, τ, z, s) = Σ_{(m,n)∈Z²} (z + mτ + n)^{-k}|z + mτ + n|^{-s}, absolutely convergent for k + Re(s) > 2 and meromorphically continued in s; E^{(k)}(τ, z) = (−1)^k (k − 1)! (2πi)^{-k} E(k, τ, z, 0) for k ≥ 1, and E^{(0)}(τ, z) = lim_{s→0} s^{-1} E(0, τ, z, s) (E(0, τ, z, s) vanishes at s = 0). For the elliptic curve E_τ = C/(Zτ + Z) with coordinate z, t = e^{2πiz}, and c ≥ 2 prime to 6: (3.8.1) for k ≥ 1, D^{k−1} dlog(cθ_E) = (c² E^{(k)}(τ, z) − c^k E^{(k)}(τ, cz)) ⊗ (dt/t)^{⊗k}; (3.8.2) log|cθ_E| = c² E^{(0)}(τ, z) − E^{(0)}(τ, cz). Transported to the lattice of a CM pair by a homothety (C/g ≅ C/(Zτ + Z) after scaling), these are the formulas used for elliptic units.
hypotheses: The series converge absolutely for k + Re(s) > 2; for k ≥ 3 the value at s = 0 is an absolutely convergent lattice sum.
The transport to an ideal lattice g by homothety is a change of variables made here, not a statement of Kato 3.8.
The normalization of cθ is the one fixed in KatoEulerSystems L0/theta-function-c-normalised.
Evaluate the analytic functions at z outside the lattice and the theta identities off E[c], so that z and cz are both outside the lattice. Lattice-point regularizations are separate from this target.
proofSteps: Kato 3.8 reviews the analytic theory: the theta function cθ is the c-smoothed Weierstrass σ-quotient, whose logarithm and logarithmic derivatives are computed by Kronecker's limit formulas.

(3.8.1)–(3.8.2) are those formulas written in the Eisenstein–Kronecker normalization. A homothety C/g ≅ C/(Zτ + Z) transports them to the lattice of a CM pair; the weights of the factors (dt/t)^{⊗k} change by the scaling factor to the k-th power, which is recorded when the formula is applied.
These identities are the input both to the Kronecker limit formula for elliptic units (15.5.1) and to the period evaluation (15.9.1).
acceptance: For k ≥ 3 the formula is an identity of absolutely convergent lattice sums.
Kato (3.8.4)(iii): for a torsion point (α, β) ≠ (0, 0), log|g_{α,β}| = E^{(0)}_{α,β}, the Siegel-unit case.

nodes.title: Kato's CM theta function aθ_E
nodes.statement: Let K′ be a field over K and E/K′ an elliptic curve with End(E) ≅ O_K, normalized so that O_K → End(E) → End_{K'}(Lie E) = K′ is the inclusion. For an ideal a of O_K prime to 6 there is a unique aθ_E ∈ O(E ∖ E[a])^× with divisor N(a)·(0) − E[a], E[a] the subgroup scheme killed by a, and with N_b(aθ_E) = aθ_E for every integer b prime to a, N_b the norm along multiplication by b. It satisfies: (15.4.1) aθ_E = cθ_E when a = (c); (15.4.2), corrected by CMAllPrimeMainConjectures/E3: the norm along an O_K-linear isogeny E → E′ of degree prime to N(a) sends aθ_E to aθ_{E′}; (15.4.3) for a, b prime to 6, (bθ_E)^{N(a)}·(pr₁^*(bθ_{E₁}))^{-1} = (aθ_E)^{N(b)}·(pr₂^*(aθ_{E₂}))^{-1} with E₁ = E/aE, E₂ = E/bE.
hypotheses: a is an integral ideal prime to 6 (so that the auxiliary integers 2 and 3 are available in the uniqueness argument).
E has CM by O_K with the normalized action. The isogeny norm identity requires an O_K-linear isogeny of degree coprime to N(a); the unrestricted assertion in the source is false.
proofSteps: Uniqueness and existence as in KatoEulerSystems L0/theta-function-c-normalised (Kato Prop. 1.3): two functions with the same divisor differ by a constant u, and invariance under N_2 and N_3 forces u^{a²−1} = 1 for a = 2, 3, hence u = 1.

Existence requires more than degree zero. Since a is prime to 6, E[a] has odd order, so pairing P with −P gives sum_{P∈E[a]} P = 0. The elliptic Pic⁰ criterion then makes N(a)(0) − E[a] principal. Carry out descent and norm normalization as in Kato Proposition 1.3 and §1.10; the normalized function is unique because a ratio u must satisfy u³ = u⁸ = 1.
(15.4.1)–(15.4.3) follow from the same 'equal divisors and N_2, N_3 invariance' argument, using the ideal isogenies E → E/aE of ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1/ideal-action.
acceptance: For a = (c) with c ∈ Z prime to 6, aθ_E is Kato's cθ_E.

nodes.title: The canonical CM pair of modulus f over K(f)
nodes.statement: Let f be a nonzero ideal of O_K with O_K^× → (O_K/f)^× injective. A CM pair of modulus f over a field K′ ⊃ K is (E, α) with E/K′ an elliptic curve with normalized O_K ≅ End(E) and α ∈ E(K′) a torsion point whose annihilator in O_K is f; isomorphisms of CM pairs are unique. (15.3.1) There is a CM pair over K(f) isomorphic over C to (C/f, 1 mod f), unique up to unique isomorphism: the canonical CM pair. (15.3.2) Every CM pair of modulus f over K′ is the base change of the canonical one along a unique K-embedding K(f) → K′. (15.3.3) For K′/K finite abelian, a an ideal prime to the ramification of K′ and σ = (a, K′/K), the conjugate pair (E^{(σ)}, σ(α)) is isomorphic to (E/aE, α mod aE), by a unique isomorphism η_a.
hypotheses: O_K^× → (O_K/f)^× is injective; for f = (1) or small f this fails and one passes to a multiple of f (Kato 15.5 takes n large).
proofSteps: Existence over C: the lattice f gives E = C/f with CM by O_K and α = 1 mod f of annihilator exactly f.

Field of definition and Galois action: the explicit reciprocity of CM theory for level structures (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.2/explicit-level-reciprocity) and the identification of the ray-level field with K(f) for the maximal order (CM.3/ray-class-values) give the model over K(f) and the formula for σ(α).
Uniqueness of isomorphisms follows from injectivity of O_K^× → (O_K/f)^×: an automorphism of E fixing α is a unit congruent to 1 mod f.

(15.3.3) is the main theorem of complex multiplication in the moduli form: conjugation by the Artin symbol of a acts on the moduli of CM pairs as the ideal action a ⋆ E = E/aE (CM.1/ideal-action), compatibly with α.
acceptance: For K = Q(i) and f = (3): O_K^× = μ_4 injects into (O_K/3)^× = F_9^×, so the canonical pair exists over K(3).

nodes.title: Standard elliptic units and their distribution relations
nodes.statement: For f with O_K^× → (O_K/f)^× injective, (E, α) the canonical CM pair over K(f) and a an ideal prime to 6f, the standard elliptic unit of modulus f and twist a is a z_f = aθ_E(α)^{-1} ∈ K(f)^×. For general m prime to a, Johnson-Leung–Kings put a ζ_m = N_{K(p^r m)/K(m)}(aθ_E(α)^{-1}) with (E, α) the canonical pair of modulus p^r m, for any r ≥ 1 with O_K^× → (O_K/p^r)^× injective; this is independent of r. Properties: (integrality) a z_f has valuation zero at every prime above 𝔭 ∤ f (it is an f-unit) and a unit when f has at least two distinct prime divisors; a ζ_{p^n} is a p-unit; (norm relation) for a prime 𝔮 with mq prime to a, N_{K(mq)/K(m)}(a ζ_{mq}) = a ζ_m^{1 − Frob_𝔮^{-1}} if 𝔮 ∤ pm and = a ζ_m if 𝔮 | pm; in particular N_{K(p^{n+1}f)/K(p^n f)}(a z_{p^{n+1}f}) = a z_{p^n f} for n large; (auxiliary independence, (15.4.4)) (b z_f)^{N(a) − σ_a} = (a z_f)^{N(b) − σ_b} for a, b prime to 6f, σ_a = (a, K(f)/K).
hypotheses: a is prime to 6f (prime to 6pf for the p-adic tower).
The Artin symbol convention is Kato's (σ_a the usual Artin symbol); Johnson-Leung–Kings' character values use η(a) = η^{-1}(σ_a).
proofSteps: Evaluate the CM theta function at the canonical torsion point; it is defined over K(f) by (15.3.2).

Integrality: compare with de Shalit's elliptic functions of Chapter II (aθ_E is a twelfth root of de Shalit's function, Johnson-Leung–Kings Prop. 3.3(1) proof); the divisor is supported on E[a], and α is not a-torsion, so the value is a unit away from primes dividing f.

Norm relation: the norm from K(mq) to K(m) of the theta value equals the theta value at the image point composed with the isogeny norm (15.4.2) and the Galois action (15.3.3); the Frobenius factor appears when q ∤ pm.
(15.4.4) from (15.4.3) and (15.3.3) applied to the isogenies E → E/aE and E → E/bE.
acceptance: The norm-compatible family (a z_{p^n f})_n defines an element of h¹ for each a prime to 6pf.

nodes.title: Kronecker's limit formula for elliptic units
nodes.statement: (15.5.1) For f with injective units, a prime to 6f and every character χ: Gal(K(f)/K) → C^×, Σ_σ χ(σ) log|σ(a z_f)| = (N(a) − χ(a)^{-1}) · lim_{s→0} s^{-1} L_{K,f}(χ, s), where L_{K,f}(χ, s) = Σ_b χ(b) N(b)^{-s} over ideals b prime to f, with χ(b) = χ((b, K(f)/K)). (15.6.5) For finite K ⊂ K′ ⊂ K(p^∞f) and the image z_{K'} ∈ (O_{K'}[1/p])^× ⊗ Q of z_{p∞f}, Σ_{σ∈Gal(K'/K)} χ(σ) log|σ(z_{K'})| = lim_{s→0} s^{-1} L_{K,pf}(χ, s) for every nontrivial χ of Gal(K′/K).
hypotheses: |·| is the absolute value through the fixed embedding K(f) ⊂ C; log|·| is extended to (O^×) ⊗ Q.
In (15.6.5) χ is nontrivial and L_{K,pf} omits the Euler factors at all primes dividing pf.
proofSteps: Apply theta-eisenstein-kronecker (3.8.2) to the lattice of the canonical CM pair and the point α, with τ ∈ K chosen as in Kato's remark after (15.5.1).

Sum over Gal(K(f)/K) using (15.3.3): conjugates of a z_f are theta values at the points of the ray classes, so the character sum becomes a partial-zeta combination equal to the leading coefficient at s = 0 of the Hecke L-series.
(15.6.5) follows by taking norms from K(p^n f) to K′ and dividing by N(a) − σ_a, using that z_{K′} only involves the modulus p^n f units, so all Euler factors at primes of pf are removed.
acceptance: For K′ = K(f) and χ ramified at every prime of f the two formulas agree up to the factor N(a) − χ(a)^{-1}.
For χ unramified at a prime 𝔩 | f with χ(𝔩) = 1, L_{K,f}(χ, s) vanishes to order at least two at s = 0 and the character sum is zero: the elliptic unit of modulus f does not see that component.

sources.match: Kronecker's limit formula for the standard elliptic unit: the character sum of log|σ(a z_f)| equals (N(a) − χ(a)^{-1}) times the derivative at 0 of the partial L-series prime to f; deduced from (3.8.2).

nodes.title: The elliptic-unit module z and the auxiliary-free element z_{p∞f}
nodes.statement: z ⊂ h¹ is the R-submodule generated by the norm-compatible families (a z_{p^n f})_{n≥1}, for n large enough that O_K^× → (O_K/p^n f)^× is injective (norm compatibility supplies the lower levels), over all ideals a of O_K prime to 6pf. For any such a ≠ O_K, N(a) − σ_a (σ_a = (a, K(p^∞f)/K)) is a non-zero-divisor of R and z_{p∞f} = (N(a) − σ_a)^{-1}·(a z_{p^n f})_n ∈ h¹ ⊗_R Q(R) ≅ H^1_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗_R Q(R) is independent of a. Moreover (N(a) − σ_a) z_{p∞f} ∈ H^1_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) for every a (15.6.3); the ideal J generated by the N(a) − σ_a is the kernel of the cyclotomic character R → Z_p (the annihilator of μ_{p^∞}(K(p^∞f))), so J_q = R_q at every height-one prime q and z_q = R_q·z_{p∞f} (15.6.4). Johnson-Leung–Kings' ζ(f) = (N(a) − σ_a)^{-1} lim_n a ζ_{fp^n} ∈ H^1(O_K[1/pf], Ω(1)) ⊗ Q(Ω) is the same element.
hypotheses: a ranges over ideals prime to 6pf; N(a) − σ_a is a non-zero-divisor exactly because its image under every character η of finite order, N(a) − η(σ_a), is nonzero.
proofSteps: Norm compatibility (standard-elliptic-unit) makes (a z_{p^n f})_n an element of h¹; R-span gives z.
Auxiliary independence (15.4.4) in the limit gives (N(b) − σ_b)(a z) = (N(a) − σ_a)(b z), so the quotient is independent of a in h¹ ⊗ Q(R).
J is generated by the N(a) − σ_a and equals the kernel of the cyclotomic character (Johnson-Leung–Kings §5.1); R/J ≅ Z_p is pseudo-null, so J is the unit ideal at height one.
Hence at height one z_q is generated by z_{p∞f}.
acceptance: ξ((h¹/z)_Q) = ξ(h¹_Q/R_Q·z_{p∞f}) in R[1/p], since z and R·z_{p∞f} differ only in codimension two.

sources.match: Defines z as the Z_p[[G_{p∞f}]]-submodule of h¹ generated by the families (a z_{p^n f})_n over a prime to 6pf.

Takes z ⊂ h¹ to be the elliptic units of Kato §15.5.

nodes.title: The elliptic units have torsion quotient
nodes.statement: For every prime p and nonzero f, h¹/z is a torsion R-module; equivalently z_{p∞f} is nonzero at every height-zero prime of R and generates h¹ there.
hypotheses: Any p, including p = 2 and primes dividing #Δ_f.
proofSteps: Height-zero primes of R correspond to pairs (a character χ of Δ up to Galois conjugacy, the generic point of the Z_p²-direction); h¹ has rank one at each (tower-unit-module-structure).

In each component choose a character η of G of finite order ramified at all primes above p and with η(Frob_𝔩) ≠ 1 for the primes 𝔩 | f, 𝔩 ∤ p, at which the component is unramified; such η exist because Frob_𝔩 has infinite order in G/I_𝔩.

Under η the image of z_{p∞f} in (O_{K'}[1/p])^× ⊗ C, K′ the field of η, has archimedean regulator equal to lim_{s→0} s^{-1}L_{K,pf}(η^{-1}, s) times a nonzero unit (kronecker-limit-formula (15.6.5)); for such η the partial L-function has a simple zero at s = 0 with nonzero leading term, by the functional equation (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation) and L(η̄, 1) ≠ 0 (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one).

The regulator map on units modulo torsion is injective (Dirichlet's unit theorem, Mathlib's regulator_ne_zero), so the η-part of z_{K′} is nonzero; hence z_{p∞f} is nonzero at the height-zero prime, and the quotient is torsion.
This is Johnson-Leung–Kings Theorem 3.9(c) (non-torsion of ζ_K(η^{-1})) in the language of h¹.
acceptance: For K = Q(i), p = 2, f = (1), R = Z_2[[Z_2²]] is a domain and the statement is that z_{2∞} ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Kato's λ-adic realization of a CM Hecke character
nodes.statement: Let r ≥ 1 and ψ a Hecke character of K of type (−r, 0) (on C^× it is z ↦ z^{−r}), L = K(ψ(K̂^×)) ⊂ C, a finite extension of K. Choose a nonzero ideal f contained in the conductor of ψ with O_K^× → (O_K/f)^× injective and let (E, α) be the canonical CM pair over K(f). Put V_L(ψ) = H^1(E(C), Q)^{⊗r} ⊗_K L (tensor power over K) and, for a finite place λ of L over p, V_{L_λ}(ψ) = H^1_ét(E ⊗ Q̄, Q_p)^{⊗r} ⊗_{K⊗Q_p} L_λ. Gal(Q̄/K(f)) acts naturally; it is extended to Gal(Q̄/K) by letting σ act as η_σ = ψ(a)^{-1}(η_a^*)^{⊗r} ∘ σ, where a is prime to f with (a, K(f)/K) = σ|_{K(f)} and η_a: (E/aE, α mod aE) ≅ (E^{(σ)}, σ(α)) is the isomorphism of (15.3.3); the result is independent of a and abelian. Under class field theory an idele a ∈ K̂^× acts as a_v^r ψ(a)^{-1} (v the place of K under λ, a_v the v-component of a), and for a prime to pf the Artin symbol (a, K(p^∞f)/K) acts as ψ(a)^{-1}; the action factors through Gal(K(p^∞f)/K). S(ψ) ⊂ coLie(E)^{⊗r} ⊗_K L is the subspace fixed by the semilinear Gal(K(f)/K)-action through η_σ, with per_ψ: S(ψ) → V_C(ψ) = V_L(ψ) ⊗ C induced by periods, and (15.8.1) S(ψ) ⊗_L L_λ ≅ D^j_dR(K ⊗ Q_p, V_{L_λ}(ψ)) for 1 ≤ j ≤ r. All constructions are independent of f up to the canonical isogenies between canonical CM pairs.
hypotheses: ψ has infinity type (−r, 0) with r ≥ 1; for a CM newform of weight k the relevant character has type (1 − k, 0), so r = k − 1.
Tensor powers ⊗^r are over K (Betti) and over K ⊗ Q_p (étale) through the CM action; in (15.8.1) the de Rham tensor power is over K ⊗ K(f).
This is the rank-one CM realization for every r ≥ 1; ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4 supplies only r = 1 (Tate-module components).
proofSteps: Fix the canonical CM pair (canonical-cm-pair) and form the tensor powers of H^1 of E with its O_K-action.

Descend the Galois action from K(f) to K with the isomorphisms η_a of (15.3.3) twisted by ψ(a)^{-1}; independence of a and commutativity follow from uniqueness of isomorphisms of CM pairs and from ψ being a character.

Identify the action by class field theory: on V_{L_λ}(ψ) an idele a acts by a_v^r ψ(a)^{-1}; for r = 1 this is CM.4/cm-hecke-character and CM.4/tate-coefficient-components, and the r-th tensor power gives the exponent r.
Define S(ψ) as Gal(K(f)/K)-invariants of the semilinear action on coLie(E)^{⊗r} ⊗_K L; the period map is the r-th tensor power of the period pairing (CM.1/cm-period-pairings).

Required geometric comparison: identify the filtered de Rham realization of H¹_ét(E) over each K(f)_w with H¹_dR(E/K(f)_w), compatibly with the CM action and tensor powers, then descend the semilinear action to obtain (15.8.1), S(ψ) ⊗_L L_λ ≅ D^j_dR(K ⊗ Q_p, V_{L_λ}(ψ)), 1 ≤ j ≤ r. Selmer L4/period-realization defines the period-ring functor but does not supply this comparison; this step is an explicit gap.
Independence of f: for f ⊂ f′ the canonical pairs are related by the canonical isogeny E″ → E″/f′E″ etc. (Kato 15.8, last paragraph).
acceptance: For r = 1 and ψ the Hecke character of a CM elliptic curve over K, V_{L_λ}(ψ) is the λ-component of the rational Tate module dual, with Frobenius at good 𝔮 ∤ pf acting by ψ(𝔮)^{-1} in Kato's geometric normalization.
dim_L V_L(ψ) = dim_L S(ψ) = 1.

nodes.title: Height-one explicit reciprocity for the CM p-divisible groups
nodes.statement: Let g = p^m f₀ (m ≥ 1, f₀ the prime-to-p part of f) with g ⊂ f and O_K^× → (O_K/g)^× injective, K′ = K(g), (E, α) the canonical CM pair over K′. E has good reduction at every finite place of K′. For a place v of K′ over p and a prime 𝔭 of O_K over p, let G(v, 𝔭) be the 𝔭-power torsion of the Néron model of E over O_v: a p-divisible group with O_𝔭-action of relative O_𝔭-height one (ordinary p-height [K_𝔭:Q_p]) over O_{K′_v}. Then the triple (K′_v, G(v, 𝔭), O_𝔭) satisfies the hypotheses of Kato's generalized explicit reciprocity law [KK3, Theorem 4.3.1] with h = 1, and that law computes the dual exponential of the Kummer image of a norm-compatible system of theta values: the image of ξ^{⊗(−r)} ⊗ (θ_n(ξ_n))_n under the cup-product/Kummer map to H^1(K′ ⊗ Q_p, (T_pE)^{⊗(−r)}(1)) followed by exp^* is p^{−mr}(r−1)!^{−1}((d/ω)^r log(θ_m))(ξ_m)·ω^{⊗r}, where ξ = (ξ_n) is the O_K ⊗ Z_p-basis of T_pE coming from the lattice g, θ_n(z) = aθ(z − ν_n) and ν_n = ξ_n − α_n.
hypotheses: The parameter h = 1 in KK3 is relative to O_𝔭. It is not ordinary p-height one at an inert or ramified prime. The source applies it to the 𝔭-divisible groups of a CM curve with good reduction.

The general theorem [KK3, Theorem 4.3.1] is not proved here; it is requested from PadicHodgeRegulators D.2, which owns Kato's big-local-field reciprocity (used with h = 2 for modular curves in Kato §10).
proofSteps: Good reduction: since g ⊂ f, Gal(K^ab/K′) acts on T_ℓE unramified outside ℓ for every ℓ, so E has good reduction everywhere over K′ (Serre–Tate criterion).

The 𝔭-divisible group of the Néron model at v is a p-divisible group of relative O_𝔭-height one (ordinary p-height two at inert or ramified p, and one for each factor at split p), so the triple satisfies [KK3]'s hypotheses with h = 1.
Apply [KK3, Theorem 4.3.1] for each v and 𝔭 and assemble over v | p, 𝔭 | p to get the stated formula for the dual exponential.
acceptance: When p splits in K the two primes 𝔭, 𝔭̄ give the two height-one factors of E[p^∞] over K′_v.

sources.match: Reduces to K′ = K(g), constructs the basis ξ, the points α_n and ν_n and the functions θ_n, notes good reduction by Serre–Tate, and applies the height-one case of [KK3, Thm. 4.3.1] to the triples (K′_v, G(v, 𝔭), O_𝔭) to compute exp^* of the Kummer images.

nodes.title: The period evaluation (15.9.1)
nodes.statement: With the notation of the proof of Prop. 15.9 (K′ = K(g), the canonical CM pair, ω a K′-basis of coLie(E), β ∈ H_1(E(C), Q) the image of 1 under K ≅ H_1(C/g, Q)), put ω_r = (r − 1)!^{-1}(d/ω)^r log(aθ)(α_m) · ω^{⊗r} ∈ S(ψ) ⊗_K K′. Then for every character χ of Gal(K′/K), Σ_{σ∈Gal(K'/K)} χ(σ) per_ψ(σ(ω_r)) = (N(a) − ψ(a)χ(a)^{-1})·L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r)·β^{⊗(−r)}, where L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, s) = Σ_b ψ̄(b)χ(b)N(b)^{-s} over ideals b prime to pf, ψ̄ the complex conjugate character (ψψ̄ = N^r). Consequently (15.9.2): for z = (N(a) − ψ(a)σ_a)^{-1}ω_r, Σ_σ χ(σ) per_ψ(σ(z)) = L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r)·β^{⊗(−r)}.
hypotheses: r ≥ 1 and ψ of type (−r, 0); the Eisenstein–Kronecker series converge absolutely only for r ≥ 3, and for r = 1, 2 the value is the analytic continuation at s = 0 (equivalently at s = r for L).
proofSteps: For σ = (b, K′/K), σ(ω_r) is the r-th logarithmic derivative of the theta function of E/bE at the image of α, transported back by η_b (15.3.3) and scaled by ψ(b)^{-1}.
Express (d/ω)^r log θ through Eisenstein–Kronecker series (theta-eisenstein-kronecker (3.8.1)): the sum over the lattice becomes a sum over c ∈ K with c ≡ 1 mod b^{-1}g of c^{−r}|c|^{−2s} at s = 0.

Re-index by the bijection c ↦ cb onto the integral ideals I prime to g in the class of b, using ψ(cJ) = c^r ψ(J) for c ∈ P(J) (ψ has type (−r, 0), so ψ((c)) = c^r for c ≡ 1 modulo the conductor), and ψ(I)ψ̄(I) = N(I)^r to turn ψ(I)^{-1}N(I)^{-s} into ψ̄(I)N(I)^{-(s+r)}; at s = 0 this is the value at r of L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, ·).
The two terms of the c-smoothing give N(a) times the sum for b and ψ(a) times the sum for ab, which assemble to (N(a) − ψ(a)χ(a)^{-1})L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r).
acceptance: For χ trivial and r ≥ 3 both sides are absolutely convergent and the identity is a rearrangement of lattice sums.

sources.match: States the period evaluation of the r-th logarithmic derivative of the theta value, with the factor N(a) − ψ(a)χ(a)^{-1}, and proves it from the Eisenstein series of 3.8 by the bijection c ↦ cJ onto ideals in a ray class.

nodes.title: Kato's explicit reciprocity law for elliptic units
nodes.statement: (Kato Prop. 15.9.) Let r ≥ 1, ψ of type (−r, 0), p a prime, f ⊂ cond(ψ) a nonzero ideal, K′ ⊂ K(p^∞f) finite over K and γ ∈ V_L(ψ). Map z_{p∞f} under H^1_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) → H^1_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗ V_L(ψ) ≅ H^1_{p∞f}(V_{L_λ}(ψ)(1)) → H^1(O_{K'}[1/p], V_{L_λ}(ψ)(1)) (the first map is x ↦ x ⊗ γ), localize at p and apply exp^* followed by (15.8.1). The image lies in S(ψ) ⊗_K K′, and for every χ: Gal(K′/K) → C^×, Σ_{σ} χ(σ)·per_ψ(σ(image)) = L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r)·γ, with L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, s) = Σ_a ψ̄(a)χ(a)N(a)^{-s} over ideals a prime to pf. For r = 1 this is the elliptic-unit reciprocity used by Burungale–Kobayashi–Ota, in their convention.
hypotheses: Every prime p, including p = 2 and p dividing #Δ_f; every r ≥ 1.
z_{p∞f} lies in the fraction module; its image becomes integral at finite level after the S-localization of (15.6.5).
proofSteps: Reduce by trace maps to K′ = K(g) with g = p^m f₀ ⊂ f and injective units (Kato's first step); by K-linearity reduce to γ = β^{⊗(−r)}.
Apply cm-p-divisible-reciprocity to the norm-compatible system (θ_n(ξ_n))_n, which is (a z_{p^n f})-type data at the shifted points; this computes exp^* of the image of a z ⊗ γ as p^{−mr} times ω_r.
Divide by N(a) − ψ(a)σ_a to remove the auxiliary ideal, and apply cm-eisenstein-evaluation (15.9.2) to obtain the character sums L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r)·γ.
The result is the same for all auxiliary choices by elliptic-unit-module (auxiliary independence).
acceptance: For χ of conductor divisible by every prime of pf, L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r) = L(ψ̄χ, r) is the full Hecke L-value; for a CM newform f attached to ψ (r = k − 1) and χ factoring through the norm, it is L(f*, χ, k − 1) up to the Euler factors at the primes of pf.
For r = 1, K = Q(i) and ψ the character of y² = x³ − x, the formula relates the localized elliptic units to the twisted values L(ψ̄χ, 1).

sources.match: States the reciprocity law for the image of z_{p∞f} under the map defined by γ, with values L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ, r)·γ, for every r ≥ 1, p, f inside the conductor of ψ and finite K′ in the tower, and proves it from [KK3, Thm. 4.3.1] with h = 1 and the evaluation (15.9.1) (page images checked).
Relies on Kato's link (15.16.1) between elliptic units and Beilinson–Kato elements, whose proof rests on this reciprocity law.

nodes.title: The Euler system of elliptic units and its twists by finite characters
nodes.statement: Fix p, an ideal a prime to 6p, and let 𝒦 be the union of the ray class fields K(q) with q prime to a. The classes a ζ_m ∈ O_{K(m)}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p ⊂ H^1(O_{K(m)}[1/p], Z_p(1)), m prime to a, form an Euler system for (𝒦, Z_p(1), pa) in Rubin's sense: for every prime 𝔮, Cor_{K(m𝔮)∩𝒦/K(m)∩𝒦}(c_{m𝔮}) = P(Frob_𝔮^{-1} | T^∨(1); Frob_𝔮^{-1}) c_m if 𝔮 ∤ m·pa and = c_m otherwise. For a character χ: G(f_χ) → E^× of conductor f_χ with a prime to f_χ, the twisted classes a ζ_m(χ) = tr_{K(f_χ m)/K(m)}(a ζ_{f_χ m} ⊗ t_p(χ)) ∈ H^1(O_{K(m)}[1/p], O_p(χ)(1)) form an Euler system for (𝒦, O_p(χ)(1), p f_χ a), and their limit along K_∞ is a ζ(χ) ∈ H^1(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1)), Λ = O_p[[Gal(K_∞/K)]]. Projection compatibility: for K ⊂ F ⊂ L ⊂ 𝒦 with G = Gal(L/F), the image of ζ_L under p_{χ^{-1}}: O_p[G] → O_p(χ) is ζ_F(χ).
hypotheses: E is a number field containing the values of χ, O_p = O_E ⊗ Z_p, t_p(χ) the canonical generator of O_p(χ) (Johnson-Leung–Kings Definition 1.1).
The Euler factors use Johnson-Leung–Kings' inverse Artin convention η(𝔮) = η(Frob_𝔮^{-1}).
proofSteps: Norm relations of standard-elliptic-unit give the Euler system axioms (Johnson-Leung–Kings Corollary 3.4), with the Euler factor 1 − Frob_𝔮^{-1} for T = Z_p(1).
Twisting by a finite-order character: Rubin's general twisting construction (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.2/twisting; Rubin 2.4.2 as cited in Johnson-Leung–Kings Proposition 3.6).

The projection formula (Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 3.7) compares corestriction with the integral character-quotient map p_{χ^{-1}} (an idempotent projection only when #G is invertible) through the formula Σ_g g(f(g^{-1}) t_p(χ)).
Norm compatibility in the K_∞-direction gives the limit class a ζ(χ).
acceptance: For χ trivial the twisted system is the elliptic-unit system itself.
a ζ(χ) is nonzero for every χ (elliptic-unit-cotorsion applied to the corresponding component).

nodes.title: The Tamagawa number conjecture at s = 0 for abelian extensions of K
nodes.statement: For an abelian extension F/K and every rational prime p, the rational (Conjecture 2.4) and integral (Conjecture 2.5) Tamagawa number conjectures hold for the motive M(F) = h^0(F)_E at s = 0. Consequently (Corollary 2.11), for abelian L ⊃ F ⊃ K, the O_p-module ⊗_η r_p(z_p(η)O_p) generated by the p-adic regulators of the zeta elements z_p(η) = ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − η(𝔭))z(η), η ∈ Ĝ_L ∖ Ĝ_F, coincides with ⊗_η Det^{-1}_{O_p} RΓ(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})(1))[1].
hypotheses: E contains the values of the characters; the Beilinson regulator (twice the Dirichlet regulator) normalizes the archimedean side (Johnson-Leung–Kings (6)).
For p = 2 the published proof rests on a preprint of Itakura; F is totally complex, so no real-place 2-torsion intervenes.
proofSteps: Both conjectures for h^0(F) at s = 0 are reformulations of the analytic class number formula with the regulator and the p-adic structure of RΓ_c (Huber–Kings Proposition 2.3.1 for p ≠ 2; Itakura 3.1 for p = 2, as cited by Johnson-Leung–Kings Theorem 2.6). The analytic class number formula is in Mathlib (the residue of the Dedekind zeta function); its passage to the integral determinant statement is the input still to be decomposed.
Pass to the quotient motive M(L)/M(F) = ⊕_{η∈Ĝ_L∖Ĝ_F} M(η) (Corollary 2.8).
Artin–Verdier duality matches the O_p-structures of RΓ_c(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})^∨) and RΓ(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})(1)) (Proposition 2.9, by Huber–Kings 1.2.10 for p ≠ 2 and Itakura 1.15 for p = 2).
Remove the Euler factors at p using Det RΓ_f(K_𝔭, O_p(η^{-1})^∨) = 1 − η(𝔭) (Corollary 2.11).
acceptance: For F = K the statement is the p-part of the class number formula for K: h_K R_K/w_K and the leading term of ζ_K at s = 0 agree up to a p-adic unit.

sources.locator: §2: Conjectures 2.4–2.5, Theorem 2.6, Corollary 2.8, Proposition 2.9, Definition 2.10 and Corollary 2.11, pp. 7–13
sources.match: Formulates the rational and integral Tamagawa number conjectures for M(F) at s = 0, records their proof for all p (Huber–Kings for p ≠ 2, Itakura for p = 2), passes to the quotient motives M(η) and reformulates the integral statement through zeta elements and determinants of RΓ(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})(1)).

nodes.title: Elliptic units are the Tamagawa zeta elements
nodes.statement: Let η: G(f_χ) → E^× have conductor f_η and level n (the largest n with K_n ⊂ K(f_η)) large enough that η is ramified at every prime above p. Then ζ_K(η^{-1}) = tr_{K(f_η)/K}(ζ_{f_η} ⊗ t_p(η^{-1})) lies in p_η(O^×_{K(f_η)} ⊗ E) = H^1_f(M(η^{-1})(1)) and equals (N a − η(a))·z_p(η); N a ≠ η(a) as automorphisms of M(η)_p for a ≠ O_K prime to 6pf_η; and r_p(z_p(η)O_p) = (N a − η(a))^{-1}ζ_K(η^{-1})O_p, so ζ_K(η^{-1}) is not torsion. Consequently, for n large enough that every η ∈ Ĝ_n(f_χ) ∖ Ĝ_{n−1}(f_χ) is ramified above p, ⊗_η (N a − η(a))^{-1}ζ_K(η^{-1})O_p = ⊗_η Det^{-1}_{O_p} RΓ(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})(1)).
hypotheses: η of large level, ramified at every prime above p, so η(𝔭) = 0 and z_p(η) = z(η).
a ≠ O_K is an ideal prime to 6pf_η.
proofSteps: Integrality: if f_η has two distinct prime factors ζ_{f_η} is a unit; otherwise f_η is a power of the unique prime above p and the p-adic valuations are killed by p_η because η is ramified at every place above p (Johnson-Leung–Kings proof of 3.9(a)).

Compute the archimedean regulator of ζ_K(η^{-1}) with kronecker-limit-formula: it equals (N a − η(a)) L^*(η, 0) t_B(η^{-1}), the regulator of (N a − η(a))z(η); injectivity of the regulator gives the identity.
N a − η(a) is invertible since η(a) is a root of unity and N a > 1.
Combine with tamagawa-s0-abelian (Corollary 2.11) for L = K_n(f_χ), F = K_{n−1}(f_χ).
acceptance: For η of small level (unramified at a prime above p) the identity acquires the Euler factor 1 − η(𝔭) and the integrality can fail; this is why the reduction to large level in lambda-main-conjecture is needed.

sources.match: For characters of large level ramified above p, the elliptic-unit class ζ_K(η^{-1}) is (N a − η(a)) times the zeta element, is integral and non-torsion, and the tensor product over new characters of these classes generates the determinant of RΓ(O_K[1/p], O_p(η^{-1})(1)).

nodes.title: Rubin's Euler-system bound for elliptic units
nodes.statement: Let η be a character of conductor f_η and level large enough that O_p(η) is ramified at every place above p, Λ_O = O_p[[Γ]], Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Z_p². Then (1) H^2(O_K[1/p], Λ(η)(1)) is Λ_O-torsion; (2) H^1(O_K[1/p], Λ(η)(1)) has Λ_O-rank one; (3) H^1/Λ_O·a ζ(η) is torsion; (4) Det H^2_0 ⊂ Det(H^1/Λ_O a ζ(η)) inside Q(Λ_O), where H^2_0 is the kernel of localization to ⊕_{v|p} H^2(K_v, Λ(η)(1)); and (Corollary 6.5) the same inclusion with H^2 in place of H^2_0. In length form: at every height-one prime 𝔮 of Λ_O, length(H^2_𝔮) ≤ length((H^1/Λ_O a ζ(η))_𝔮). By twisting (Lemma 6.1) the inequality holds for every χ at height-one primes, which is Rubin's inequality, Kato Theorem 15.2(1), in the form needed at regular primes.
hypotheses: Every prime p, including p = 2 and 3; Rubin's hypotheses Hyp(K_∞/K) and Hyp(K_∞, O_p(η)(1)) hold with τ = 1 because K is imaginary quadratic and the coefficient module has rank one.
The local H^2(K_v, Λ(η)(1)), v | p, are finitely generated O_p-modules, hence pseudo-null (Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.6).
proofSteps: Check Rubin's hypotheses for the Z_p²-extension K_∞ (no finite prime splits completely: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.8/admissible-zp-d-extension, ES.8/leopoldt-tower-hypothesis, ES.8/iwasawa-large-image-hypotheses).

The Λ-adic class a ζ(η) is non-torsion (elliptic-zeta-element-comparison), so Rubin's Theorem II.3.2 gives torsion of X_∞ = H^2_0 (ES.8/weak-leopoldt-from-an-euler-system), and with Lemma 4.6 torsion of H^2.
Rank one of H^1 from the Euler characteristic rank H^1 − rank H^2 = 1 (r₂(K) = 1) and H^0 = 0.

Rubin's Theorem II.3.3, ind_Λ(c) ⊂ char(X_∞) (ES.8/rubin-iwasawa-divisibility), together with the pseudo-isomorphism H^1 → Λ_O ⊕ torsion, gives the determinant inclusion (Johnson-Leung–Kings proof of 6.4(4)).
Corollary 6.5: H^2_0 and H^2 have the same characteristic ideal because the local H^2 at p are pseudo-null.
acceptance: The inclusion is integral, with no power of p lost, for every p including 2.

sources.locator: Definition 6.3, Theorem 6.4, Corollary 6.5, pp. 30–31; Lemma 4.6, p. 22
sources.match: For characters of large level, the Euler-system theory gives torsion of H², rank one of H¹, torsion of H¹ modulo the elliptic-unit class and the determinant inclusion, first for H²_0 and then, the local terms at p being pseudo-null, for H².
Rubin's inequality length(h²_𝔭) ≤ length((h¹/z)_𝔭) at height-one primes not containing p (condition (a)).
Rubin's Iwasawa-theoretic Euler-system theorems: weak Leopoldt and the divisibility char(X_∞) | ind_Λ(c).

nodes.title: The main conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields at every prime (Johnson-Leung–Kings Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: For every prime p and every character χ: G(f_χ) → E^× of conductor f_χ, with Λ_O = O_p[[Gal(K_∞/K)]]: (1) H^0(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1)) = 0; (2) H^1(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1)) has Λ_O-rank one and H^1/J_Λ(ζ(χ)) is torsion; (3) H^2(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1)) is torsion; and the inclusion κ_χ: J_Λ(ζ(χ)) → RΓ(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1))[1] is good in the sense of Knudsen–Mumford with Div(κ_χ) = 0, so that κ_χ induces Det_{Λ_O}(H^1/J_Λ(ζ(χ))) ≅ Det_{Λ_O} H^2. Here ζ(χ) = (N a − σ_a)^{-1} a ζ(χ) ∈ H^1 ⊗ Q(Λ_O) and J_Λ is the kernel of the cyclotomic character Λ → Z_p. In length form: length((H^1/J_Λζ(χ))_𝔮) = length(H^2_𝔮) at every height-one prime 𝔮 of Λ_O, integrally, including 𝔮 ∋ p.
hypotheses: No restriction on p: Johnson-Leung–Kings say the theorem holds for all primes with no exceptions, removing Rubin's condition that p not divide the degree of the abelian field cut out by χ; in particular p = 2 and 3 are covered, which Rubin's standing hypothesis p ∤ #μ(H) excludes.
The p = 2 case rests on tamagawa-s0-abelian at p = 2 (Itakura's preprint, a recorded gap).
proofSteps: Reduce to characters of large level by twisting with a continuous ρ: Γ → O_p^× (Lemmas 4.7 and 6.1, Corollary 6.2); the statement is invariant under such twists.

For η of large level: Div(κ_η ∘ τ_η) is effective by elliptic-unit-euler-system-bound, and Div(τ_η) is effective with (N a − σ_a)^{-1}Det(Λ_O a ζ(η)) = Det(J_Λ ζ(η)) (Lemma 6.6, using that J_Λ ζ(η)/... is pseudo-null), so Div(κ_η) is effective.

Effective divisors vanish when their sum over all new characters η of level n vanishes; test the resulting inclusion of invertible modules after the augmentation ι: Λ_O → O_p (Nakayama). By Lemma 6.7 and the identity (N a − σ_a) ↦ N a − η^{-1}(a), the pulled-back inclusion becomes the inclusion of elliptic-zeta-element-comparison, which is an equality by the Tamagawa input.
Hence Div(κ_η) = 0 for all η of large level and, by step 1, for every χ.
acceptance: For χ trivial and p ∤ 6 split in K, the statement contains the one-variable and two-variable classical main conjectures of Rubin in their cohomological form.
K = Q(i), p = 2, χ = 1: the equality holds integrally over Z_2[[Z_2²]].

sources.match: States the Λ-main conjecture for every character and every prime with no exceptions, and proves it by reduction to large level, the Euler-system divisibility, Lemma 6.6 and the augmentation argument with Corollary 3.10.
The Knudsen–Mumford functors Det and Div and the good maps used to state the equality.

nodes.title: The main conjecture over O_K[1/pf] with Euler factors
nodes.statement: Suppose f_χ | f and put ζ(χ, f) = ∏_{𝔩|f, 𝔩∤p}(1 − χ(𝔩)Frob_𝔩^{-1})·ζ(χ) (image in H^1(O_K[1/pf], Λ(χ)(1))). Then J_Λ(ζ(χ, f)) → RΓ(O_K[1/pf], Λ(χ)(1))[1] is good and induces Det_{Λ_O}(H^1(O_K[1/pf], Λ(χ)(1))/J_Λ(ζ(χ, f))) ≅ Det_{Λ_O} H^2(O_K[1/pf], Λ(χ)(1)).
hypotheses: Every prime p; f_χ | f.
χ(𝔩) = 0 when χ is ramified at 𝔩, so the factor is 1 there.
proofSteps: Combine lambda-main-conjecture with the localization triangle relating O_K[1/p] and O_K[1/pf].

The supported complexes at 𝔩 | f, 𝔩 ∤ p have determinant Λ_O(1 − χ(𝔩)Frob_𝔩^{-1})^{-1} (h2-euler-comparison; Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.3), which is exactly compensated by the Euler factors in ζ(χ, f).
acceptance: If every prime of f divides p, ζ(χ, f) = ζ(χ) and the statement is lambda-main-conjecture.

sources.match: The main conjecture over O_K[1/pf] with the elliptic-unit element multiplied by the Euler factors at the primes of f prime to p, from the localization sequence and Lemma 4.3.

nodes.title: Rubin's Iwasawa modules U_∞, Ē_∞, C̄_∞, A_∞, X_∞
nodes.statement: Fix a prime 𝔭 of K above p, an abelian extension K₀ of K containing the Hilbert class field H with p ∤ [K₀ : K], and an abelian extension K_∞ of K containing K₀ with Gal(K_∞/K₀) ≅ Z_p or Z_p²; G = Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Δ × Γ with Δ = Gal(K₀/K). For finite F ⊂ K_∞ over K: A(F) is the p-part of the class group, ℰ(F) the global units, 𝒞(F) Rubin's elliptic units of F, U(F) the local units of F ⊗ K_𝔭 congruent to 1 modulo the primes above 𝔭, Ē(F) and C̄(F) the closures of ℰ(F) ∩ U(F) and 𝒞(F) ∩ U(F) in U(F), and X(F) = Gal(M(F)/F) for M(F) the maximal abelian p-extension of F unramified outside the primes above 𝔭. A_∞, U_∞, Ē_∞, C̄_∞, X_∞ are the norm limits, modules over Λ = Z_p[[G]] = ⊕_χ Λ^χ, χ running over the irreducible Z_p-representations of Δ, Λ^χ ≅ R_χ[[Γ]] (R_χ the unramified extension of Z_p of degree dim χ). Global class field theory gives the exact sequence 0 → Ē_∞/C̄_∞ → U_∞/C̄_∞ → X_∞ → A_∞ → 0.
hypotheses: Rubin's standing hypothesis: p does not divide the number of roots of unity in H (so p > 2, and p > 3 when 3 ramifies in K), and p ∤ [K₀ : K].
Rubin's 𝒞(F) is generated by elliptic units of all moduli dividing the conductor; up to torsion C_∞ is the Ω-span of I_Ω J_Ω(ζ(g)) for all g | f (Johnson-Leung–Kings §5.4).
proofSteps: Form the finite-level modules and their limits under norms; the χ-decomposition uses the idempotents e_χ, which are integral since p ∤ #Δ.

The exact sequence (5) is the limit of the class-field-theoretic sequences at finite level, comparing the 𝔭-ramified Galois group with local units modulo global units and the class group. Use the finite-level sequences from ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 and the exactness of inverse limits of compact Hausdorff modules; a cyclotomic-plus exact sequence from Selmer L4/unit-class-sequence does not itself imply this CM-tower sequence.
Compare with Johnson-Leung–Kings §5.4: E′_∞ ≅ H^1(O_K[1/p], Ω(1)) and the sequence of Lemma 5.8 linking E_∞, E′_∞, the decomposition-group modules, A_∞ and H^2(O_K[1/p], Ω(1)).
acceptance: When p does not split in K, X_∞ and U_∞/C̄_∞ are not torsion Λ-modules (Rubin, Remark 2 after Theorem 4.1); when p splits they are torsion and the two equalities of Theorem 4.1(i) are equivalent through (5).

sources.match: The standing hypothesis on p, the fields K₀ ⊂ K_∞, the modules A, ℰ, 𝒞, U, Ē, C̄, X and their limits, the decomposition Λ = ⊕Λ^χ and the exact sequence (5).
The relation of the classical modules E_∞, E′_∞, A_∞, C_∞ to the cohomological ones.

nodes.title: Rubin's main conjecture and its all-prime classical form
nodes.statement: (Rubin, Theorem 4.1) Under Rubin's hypotheses: (i) if p splits in K, char(A_∞) = char(Ē_∞/C̄_∞) and char(X_∞) = char(U_∞/C̄_∞); (ii) if p is inert or ramified in K, char(A_∞) divides char(Ē_∞/C̄_∞), with equality of χ-parts char(A_∞)^χ = char(Ē_∞/C̄_∞)^χ for every irreducible χ of Δ that is nontrivial on the decomposition group of 𝔭 in Δ. (Johnson-Leung–Kings §5.4) When p ∤ #Δ, for every prime p (2 and 3 included) and every χ, Det_{Λ_O}(p_{χ^{-1}}E_∞/I_Λ J_Λ(ζ(χ))) ≅ Det_{Λ_O}(p_{χ^{-1}}A_∞), i.e. char(p_{χ^{-1}}A_∞) = char(p_{χ^{-1}}E_∞/I_Λ J_Λ(ζ(χ))), integrally, with no condition on the splitting of p or on χ.
hypotheses: Rubin's statement: p ∤ #μ(H) and p ∤ [K₀ : K]; Johnson-Leung–Kings' classical form: p ∤ #Δ only.
The statements are integral equalities of ideals of Λ, not after inverting p.
proofSteps: Rubin proves (i) and (ii) by Kolyvagin–Thaine methods (Rubin §§8–10, case table p. 58); for nonsplit p only the divisibility in general, equality on χ nontrivial on the decomposition group.

For the all-prime form: decompose Ω_O = ∏_χ Λ(χ) (possible since p ∤ #Δ), identify p_{χ^{-1}}E′_∞ with H^1(O_K[1/p], Λ(χ)(1)) (rubin-iwasawa-modules), and use Lemma 5.8's sequence: the decomposition-group modules at p are pseudo-null, so H^2 and A_∞ have the same characteristic ideal and E′_∞ and E_∞ differ by pseudo-null terms after the augmentation ideal I_Λ.
Apply lambda-main-conjecture to get the determinant isomorphism.
acceptance: Consumers needing the inert-prime anticyclotomic input (Agboola–Howard II Proposition 3.3(ii), used by InertAnticyclotomicCMMainConjecture) obtain it from the χ-part equality (ii), as Agboola–Howard do; an inert-prime 'units form' char(X_∞^χ) = char(U_∞^χ/C̄_∞^χ) is not a theorem of Rubin, since those modules are not torsion.
For K = Q(i), p = 5 (split), f = (1): Δ ≅ Z/4 has order prime to 5 and both forms apply.

nodes.title: The two-variable Coleman map at a split prime
nodes.statement: Unverified construction target (exact source and coefficient extension required): Let p = 𝔭𝔭̄ split in K, under Rubin's hypotheses (p ∤ #μ(H)), with K₀ ⊃ H abelian over K, p ∤ [K₀ : K], and K_∞ ⊃ K₀ abelian over K with Gal(K_∞/K₀) ≅ Z_p², as in rubin-iwasawa-modules. Let Ô be the ring of integers of the completion of the maximal unramified extension of K_𝔭 = Q_p and F the relative Lubin–Tate formal group over Ô attached to the CM curve at 𝔭 (height one). The two-variable Coleman map is the Λ-linear map Col: U_∞ → Λ_Ô = Ô[[G]] obtained by interpolating norm-compatible local units by Coleman power series for F, taking the logarithmic derivative, and Mellin-transforming the resulting measure on the Tate module of F; it is injective on each χ-part with pseudo-null (indeed explicitly computable) cokernel, so char(U_∞^χ/C̄_∞^χ) = char(Λ_Ô^χ/Col(C̄_∞^χ)) after extending scalars to Ô.
hypotheses: p splits in K and p ∤ #μ(H); the construction is local at 𝔭 and uses the CM formal group of height one.
Scalars are extended to Ô, faithfully flat over Z_p, so characteristic ideals can be compared after extension.

The strong integral map, kernel/cokernel and restriction assertions below are unverified targets, not checked consequences of Rubin Remark (1). Specify the completed coefficient extension of U_∞ before comparing its rank or cokernel with Ô[[G]].
proofSteps: Coleman's interpolation of norm-compatible units by power series, for the height-one relative Lubin–Tate group F of the CM curve at 𝔭 (the cyclotomic case is ColemanPowerSeries L1; the relative height-one version over Ô is requested there).
The operator (1 − φ/p)·dlog turns the Coleman series into a measure on Z_p^× ≅ T_𝔭F-units, and descending along the 𝔭̄-direction of the tower gives a measure on G.
Identify kernel and cokernel on χ-parts: they are controlled by the torsion of F over the tower and by the roots of unity, which are pseudo-null for the two-variable algebra under Rubin's hypotheses.
acceptance: For the one-variable cyclotomic analogue over Q_p this is ColemanPowerSeries L2's Coleman map, with the same sign convention to be fixed.

nodes.title: Elliptic units map to Katz's two-variable measure
nodes.statement: Unverified image target (not implied by a characteristic-ideal identity alone): In the setting of two-variable-coleman-map, Col(C̄_∞) is the Λ_Ô-submodule generated by Katz's two-variable p-adic L-function (measure) μ_𝔭 on G, restricted to its χ-parts and with the Euler factors at the primes of the conductor removed as in Rubin's definition of 𝒞; consequently char(U_∞^χ/C̄_∞^χ) = (L_𝔭^χ), the χ-part of Katz's measure, as ideals of Λ_Ô^χ.

Equality of Col(C̄_∞) with a generated measure module is stronger than equality of characteristic ideals; the former has not been verified from the sources read.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic θ-components and the λ-invariant equality
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split in K as v v̄, K_∞ the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension, Λ = Z_p[[Gal(K_∞/K)]] (scalars extended as needed), and θ: G_K → F_p^× a character (lifted by Teichmüller to Z_p^×) whose conductor is divisible only by primes split in K, with θ|_{G_v̄} ≠ 1, ω. Let K_θ be its fixed field, Δ_θ = Gal(K_θ/K), M_θ = Z_p(θ) ⊗ Λ^∨, Σ a finite set of places containing ∞, the primes above p and the conductor of θ, all finite ones split, and 𝔛_∞ = Gal(M_∞/K_∞K_θ) for M_∞ the maximal abelian pro-p extension of K_∞K_θ unramified outside v. Restriction gives H^1(K^Σ/K, M_θ) ≅ H^1(K^Σ/K_θ, M_θ)^{Δ_θ} ≅ Hom_cts((𝔛^Σ_∞)^θ, Q_p/Z_p), 𝔛^Σ_∞ the Σ-ramified Galois group; imposing the Greenberg local conditions (unramified away from p, relaxed at v, strict at v̄) gives H^1_{F_Gr}(K, M_θ) ≅ Hom_cts(𝔛_∞^θ, Q_p/Z_p). Then char_Λ(𝔛_∞^θ) = (L_θ), the θ-branch anticyclotomic projection of Katz's measure; in particular 𝔛_∞^θ is torsion and λ(𝔛_θ) = λ(L_θ). For a branch tamely ramified at p, L_θ means the projection of Katz's measure on Gal(K(𝔠p^∞)/K) along the branch character (the convention of PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E3, not stated in Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner).
hypotheses: p > 2 split in K; p never divides #O_K^× then, since 3 ramifies in Q(√−3).
θ has order prime to p, conductor supported on split primes, and θ|_{G_v̄} ≠ 1, ω (Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner's hypothesis in Theorem 1.2.2).
μ = 0 for L_θ is Hida's theorem, owned by AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3h; it is not needed for the λ-equality but is part of Theorem 1.2.2.
proofSteps: Restriction to K_θ is an isomorphism onto Δ_θ-invariants since p ∤ #Δ_θ, and Shapiro's lemma identifies H^1(K^Σ/K_θ, M_θ)^{Δ_θ} with the dual of the θ-part of the Σ-ramified Galois group (Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner (1.4), where the Δ_θ-invariants are omitted; PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E16). The Greenberg local conditions cut out the Selmer group, which corresponds to the quotient 𝔛_∞^θ ramified only at v (their Proposition 1.1.3 and the unramified-condition comparison).

Apply katz-form-main-conjecture to the one-variable anticyclotomic tower over K₀ = K_θ·H. Rubin's hypothesis p ∤ [K₀ : K] holds when p ∤ h_K (θ has order prime to p); when p | h_K it fails and the input is the recorded gap 'Split-prime Katz form when p divides the class number'.

For a branch θ tamely ramified at p, define L_θ as the projection of Katz's measure on the ray tower of conductor 𝔠p^∞ along θ, as PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E3 requires; the main conjecture is then a statement about that element.
λ-equality: characteristic ideals generate the same principal ideal, so their λ-invariants agree.
acceptance: Consumer: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.7a (Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner Theorem 2.2.3, which uses λ(L_φ) = λ(𝔛_φ) and λ(L_ψ) = λ(𝔛_ψ) for ψ = φ^{-1}ω).

nodes.title: Functional equation of the anticyclotomic Katz projections and λ(L_ψ) = λ(L_φ)
nodes.statement: In the setting of anticyclotomic-theta-main-conjecture, the λ-invariants of the anticyclotomic Katz projections along θ and along θ^{-1}ω agree: λ(L_θ) = λ(L_{θ^{-1}ω}). In particular, for ψ = φ^{-1}ω, λ(L_ψ) = λ(L_φ). Only the λ-invariants are asserted; the precise relation between the two projections is the functional equation of Katz's measure, which is requested from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3.
hypotheses: θ and θ^{-1}ω both satisfy the hypotheses of the anticyclotomic node, or the tamely ramified branch convention of PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E3 is used for the one that is ramified at p.
proofSteps: The functional equation of Katz's two-variable measure relates the measure at a character and at its dual twisted by the norm, which on the anticyclotomic line is θ ↦ θ^{-1}ω composed with the inversion of the anticyclotomic variable (request to AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3; Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner cite Kriz 2016, Theorem 27).

The involution of Λ induced by γ ↦ γ^{-1} preserves λ-invariants, as Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner note; whatever unit or Euler factors the functional equation introduces must be checked to have λ-invariant zero when the supplier states it.
acceptance: Applied in Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner (2.11), p. 15.

sources.match: Since ψ = φ^{-1}ω, the functional equation of Katz's p-adic L-function gives λ(L_ψ) = λ(L_φ).

Only regular primes (p ∉ q); Johnson-Leung–Kings' singular-prime argument (§7.3) needs a μ-invariant hypothesis that is not assumed and is not needed here.

nodes.title: Three characterizations of CM newforms
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized newform, k ≥ 2. The following are equivalent: (a) f has a nontrivial self-twist in the sense of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 9 (f is the primitive form of f ⊗ χ for some Dirichlet character χ ≠ 1); (b) f has CM in Kato's sense: there are an imaginary quadratic K and a continuous Hecke character ψ of K with L(f, s) = L(ψ, s); (c) f is the newform θ_ψ attached to an algebraic Hecke character ψ of an imaginary quadratic K of infinity type (1 − k, 0). In that case χ = ε_K is the quadratic character of K, ψ in (b) may be replaced by ψ∘c to have type (1 − k, 0), the conductor f_ψ satisfies N = |d_K|·N(f_ψ), the nebentypus is determined by ψ and ε_K, and the Hecke field F is contained in L = K(ψ(K̂^×)).
hypotheses: Normalized newform of weight k ≥ 2 and level N; the self-twist predicate is the one of ModularForms Layer 9, not a second definition.
Burungale–Tian's proofs need only the direction from ψ to f; the equivalence is the interface with Kato §15 and with the non-CM branch of Kato 12.8.
proofSteps: (c) ⇒ (b): the L-function of the theta series of ψ is L(ψ, s) (Hecke), with level |d_K|N(f_ψ). The level formula and the nebentypus are the classical theta-series computation; they are not stated in the cited places of Kato or Burungale–Tian, and their source (Hecke, Shimura) was not read here.

(b) ⇒ (a): comparing Euler factors, a_ℓ(f) = 0 for ℓ inert in K, so f and f ⊗ ε_K have the same Hecke eigenvalues away from the level and the same primitive form (strong multiplicity one, ModularForms Layer 5 via Layer 9).

(a) ⇒ (c): Ribet's theorem (Kato's [Ri2]): a nontrivial self-twist χ is quadratic, cuts out an imaginary quadratic K, and V(f) ⊗ χ ≅ V(f) makes V(f) induced from a character of G_K, which is algebraic of type (1 − k, 0) by Hodge–Tate weights; its L-function is L(f, s). Ribet's LNM 601 was not read for this design (gap).
The conductor and Hecke-field statements follow from (c) and the formula for the level of a theta series.
acceptance: The newform 32.2.a.a (y² = x³ − x) has CM by Q(i): ψ of conductor (1+i)^3, |d_K| N(f_ψ) = 4·8 = 32.
The newform 27.2.a.a has CM by Q(√−3): ψ of conductor (3) = (√−3)², and |d_K|·N(f_ψ) = 3·9 = 27.
11.2.a.a has no CM: a CM form of level 11 would need |d_K| dividing 11, so K = Q(√−11); 2 is inert in Q(√−11) since −11 ≡ 5 mod 8, but a_2 = −2 ≠ 0.

sources.match: For a CM newform of weight k, L(s, f) = L(s, ψ) for a Hecke character of the CM field of type (1 − k, 0).

Kato's definition of CM (equality with the L-function of a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field), and for CM f a character ψ of type (1 − k, 0) whose conductor divides N, with F ⊂ L and V_{L_λ}(f) induced from V_{L_λ}(ψ) by comparing Frobenius polynomials, citing Ribet. The level formula N = |d_K|N(f_ψ) is not stated there.

nodes.title: Kato's Galois normalization of the CM induction (Lemma 15.11(1))
nodes.statement: Let f be a CM newform attached to ψ of type (1 − k, 0) and conductor f_ψ, L = K(ψ(K̂^×)), r = k − 1. Assume the Galois isomorphism V_{L_λ}(f) ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q} V_{L_λ}(ψ) (Kato 15.10, requested from ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4) and fix an L-isomorphism (15.11.1) S(ψ) ≅ S(f) ⊗_F L. Then for each finite λ there is a unique G_Q-isomorphism (15.11.2) V_{L_λ}(f) ≅ Ind V_{L_λ}(ψ) =: V~_{L_λ}(ψ) such that the composite S(ψ) ⊗ L_λ ≅ D^r_dR(V_{L_λ}(ψ)) ≅ D^r_dR(V_{L_λ}(f)) ≅ S(f) ⊗ L_λ is induced by (15.11.1). This is the identification of Galois modules used throughout; the archimedean normalization (15.11.3) is CZ.6/cm-period-normalization and is never used as a Galois identification.

proofSteps: Any G_Q-isomorphism h induces an isomorphism S(ψ) ⊗ L_λ ≅ S(f) ⊗ L_λ of one-dimensional spaces, equal to c times (15.11.1) for some c ∈ L_λ^×; take c^{-1}h.
Uniqueness: an automorphism of the irreducible representation V~_{L_λ}(ψ) is a scalar, and the de Rham condition fixes the scalar.

nodes.title: Nonvanishing of cyclotomic twists of CM L-values (Kato 13.5 for CM forms)
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized newform of weight k ≥ 2 (in particular a CM newform, L(f, χ, s) = L(ψ·(χ∘N_{K/Q}), s)). (1) L(f, χ, s) has no zero in Re(s) ≥ (k + 1)/2 for every Dirichlet character χ. (2) (Rohrlich) If k is even and P is a finite set of primes, then L(f, χ, k/2) ≠ 0 for all but finitely many primitive Dirichlet characters χ unramified outside P and ∞; the same holds for the S-imprimitive values L_S(f, χ, k/2) with S finite. Consequently, for each height-zero prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] (a sign and a branch character), infinitely many finite-order characters χ in that component have L_S(f*, χ, k − 1) = L_S(ψ̄, χ∘N_{K/Q}, k − 1) ≠ 0.
hypotheses: For k ≥ 3, s = k − 1 lies in Re(s) ≥ (k + 1)/2 and (1) suffices; for k = 2, s = 1 = k/2 is central and (2) is needed.
Rohrlich's Theorem 1 is for any newform of even weight k, any character and level; the proof combines his 1984 method with Jacquet–Langlands' twisted root numbers and was not decomposed here (gap).
proofSteps: (1): Kato states Jacquet–Shalika for L(f, s); the twist f ⊗ χ is a cusp form of weight k whose newform differs from it by finitely many Euler factors, nonvanishing in Re(s) ≥ (k+1)/2, so the statement holds for L(f, χ, s). For a CM form, L(f, χ, s) is a Hecke L-function of K and nonvanishing on the edge is Hecke's theorem; the finite-order case is AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one and the unitary infinite-order case is requested from AN.4.
(2): Rohrlich 1988, Theorem 1.

For the components: a height-zero prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] fixes the restriction to the torsion part and the sign; within it the characters of p-power conductor are infinite in number, and by (1) or (2) all but finitely many have nonvanishing value at s = k − 1.
acceptance: For f = 32.2.a.a and p = 2, infinitely many even (resp. odd) characters of 2-power conductor have L(f, χ, 1) ≠ 0.

sources.match: (1) no zero on Re(s) ≥ (k+1)/2 (Jacquet–Shalika); (2) for even k and finite S, finitely many characters with conductor in S have L_S(f, χ, k/2) = 0 (Rohrlich [Ro2]).
For even k and a normalized newform of any character and level, L(k/2, f, χ) ≠ 0 for all but finitely many primitive Dirichlet characters unramified outside a fixed finite set of primes.
Uses 13.5 with (15.12.2) to see that the elliptic-unit class is nonzero at each height-zero prime.

nodes.title: Kato's CM comparison map (15.12.1)
nodes.statement: For a finite place λ of L, the O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]-linear map (15.12.1) H^1_{p∞f}(V_{L_λ}(ψ)) → H^1(V_{L_λ}(f)) defined as follows: by Shapiro and (15.11.2), H^1(V_{L_λ}(f)) = H^1(V~_{L_λ}(ψ)) = lim_n H^1(O_K ⊗ Z[ζ_{p^n}, 1/p], T) ⊗ Q for any Gal(Q̄/K)-stable O_λ-lattice T of V_{L_λ}(ψ); and the inclusions K ⊗ Q(ζ_{p^n}) ⊂ K(p^n f) give corestriction maps from the ray tower to the cyclotomic tower over K. Module structures are compatible through the restriction O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] → O_λ[[G_∞]] (or O_λ[[G′_∞]] when K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞})).
hypotheses: f is a CM newform attached to ψ with f ⊂ cond(ψ) (one takes f = cond(ψ) for the main theorem).
H^1(V(f)) is Kato's cyclotomic Iwasawa cohomology of V_{F_λ}(f) ⊗ L_λ with the j_* convention.
proofSteps: Shapiro's lemma identifies the cohomology of the induced representation over Q with that of V(ψ) over K, layer by layer along Q(ζ_{p^n}).
Corestriction from K(p^n f) to K(ζ_{p^n}) (the compositum K·Q(ζ_{p^n}) is inside K(p^n f)) gives the map on each layer; compatibility with the transition maps gives the limit.
The identification of coefficients uses (15.11.2) only (cm-induction-normalization).
acceptance: Composing with the specialization at a finite-order character of G_∞ gives the finite-level corestriction to K(ζ_{p^n}).

nodes.title: Twisting the tower cohomology to CM coefficients
nodes.statement: Let ψ have conductor f, T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ) a stable O_λ-lattice and χ_T: G_{p∞f} → O_λ^× the character by which Gal(Q̄/K) acts on T(−1) (it factors through G_{p∞f}). (a) There is a canonical isomorphism H^q_{p∞f}(T) ≅ (H^q_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗_{Z_p} O_λ) ⊗ T(−1), with natural left deck action and diagonal action on the tensor product. For a chosen basis t of T(−1), the map φ_t from the untwisted module to H^q(T), x ↦ x ⊗ t, obeys φ_t(rx) = Tw_{χ_T^{-1}}(r)φ_t(x), where Tw_χ(g) = χ(g)g. Its inverse is Tw_{χ_T}-semilinear, carrying z ⊗ O_λ to the span of z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) at height one. (b) H^1_{p∞f}(T) is torsion-free with localization of rank one at every height-zero prime, and H^1_{p∞f}(V_{L_λ}(ψ))_q is free of rank one over O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q at every height-one prime q lying over a height-zero prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] (the form used in Kato 15.15).
hypotheses: T(−1) is unramified outside pf, so its action factors through G_{p∞f}; the twist is the continuous character χ_T.
proofSteps: The Galois module T is Z_p(1) ⊗ T(−1) with T(−1) a character of G_{p∞f}; the twisting isomorphism of ray-tower-iwasawa-cohomology (Johnson-Leung–Kings Lemma 4.7) gives (a).
The element z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) corresponds to z under (a) (Kato (15.6.4) after the twist).

(b) is the twist of tower-unit-module-structure (torsion-free, generic rank one) and tower-kummer-identification. At height-one primes q lying over height-zero primes of the cyclotomic algebra, p ∉ q and the localized ring is a discrete valuation ring (q regular), so a torsion-free module of rank one is free of rank one there; Kato 15.15 asserts this freeness.
acceptance: For ψ the character of y² = x³ − x and p = 2, T = T_2E-component, the twist χ_T is the 2-adic character of the curve composed with the cyclotomic inverse.

sources.match: Uses that H^1_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q is free of rank one and the module A·(z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1)).
The Galois action on O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] by multiplication by the image of σ^{-1}, which fixes the sign of the twist.
Twisting Iwasawa cohomology by a continuous character.

nodes.title: Kato's descent from the ray tower to the cyclotomic tower (Lemma 15.13)
nodes.statement: Assume K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}). Let f be the conductor of ψ, Δ the torsion subgroup of G_{p∞f}, λ | p, 𝔭 a prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] and q its inverse image under the surjection O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] → O_λ[[G_∞]]. If 2 and #Δ are invertible in the residue field of 𝔭, then (1) O_λ[[G_∞]]_𝔭 and O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q are regular local rings and the kernel of O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q → O_λ[[G_∞]]_𝔭 is principal, generated by some a; (2) for every stable lattice T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ) and T~ = Ind_K^Q T: (15.13.1) H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q/a ≅ H^2(T~)_𝔭, and (15.13.2) 0 → H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q/a → H^1(T~)_𝔭 → H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q[a] → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}); 2 and #Δ invertible in the residue field at 𝔭 — automatic when p ∉ 𝔭, since that residue field has characteristic zero; this is all Burungale–Tian's rational setting secures (footnote 4), not the hypothesis K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}) (PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/E13).
The H^2[a] term is retained; specialization is not assumed exact.
proofSteps: Regularity: the residue characteristic condition makes the group rings of Δ étale at 𝔭, so both localizations are localizations of power series rings over O_λ; the kernel of the restriction map is generated by one element because G_{p∞f} → G_∞ has kernel of Z_p-rank one modulo Δ.
The short exact sequence 0 → T ⊗ O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] →(a) T ⊗ O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] → T ⊗ O_λ[[G_∞]] → 0, with σ acting through σ^{-1}.

Inertia at v ∤ p acts on T ⊗ O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]] through Δ, so the cokernel of the invariants is killed by #Δ; hence the j_*-sequences give the long exact sequence after localization at q, which splits into (15.13.1) and (15.13.2) by Shapiro (T ⊗ O_λ[[G_∞]] computes H^q(T~)).
acceptance: For K = Q(√−7) and p = 5 the hypothesis K ⊄ Q(μ_{5^∞}) holds and the lemma applies at every 𝔭 with 2#Δ invertible.

sources.match: Regularity and principality of the kernel at q, and the descent isomorphism (15.13.1) and exact sequence (15.13.2), proved from the exact coefficient sequence and the inertia invariants being controlled by #Δ.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6 and footnote 4, p. 5

nodes.title: Descent when the CM field lies in the cyclotomic tower (Kato 15.14)
nodes.statement: Assume K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}); this happens exactly for K = Q(√−p) with p ≡ 3 mod 4, and for p = 2 with K = Q(i) or Q(√−2) (an elementary classification of the imaginary quadratic subfields of Q(μ_{p^∞}), not stated by Kato). Put G′_∞ = Gal(Q(μ_{p^∞})/K) ⊂ G_∞ and H^q(T) = lim_n H^q(Z[ζ_{p^n}, 1/p], T) for a stable lattice T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ). Then H^q(T~) ≅ H^q(T) ⊗_{O_λ[[G′_∞]]} O_λ[[G_∞]], and Lemma 15.13 holds with G_∞ replaced by G′_∞ and H^q(T~) by H^q(T): regularity, principality of the kernel a, (15.13.1) and (15.13.2).
hypotheses: K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}); the residue-field condition on 2 and #Δ as in Lemma 15.13.
This is the case of the congruent-number application (K = Q(i), p = 2) and of the cube-sum application (K = Q(√−3), p = 3); it is not an excluded corner case.
proofSteps: K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}) means the image of G_{p∞f} in the cyclotomic group is the index-two subgroup G′_∞, and Ind from K to Q of cohomology over Q(μ_{p^n}) ⊃ K is base change along O_λ[[G′_∞]] → O_λ[[G_∞]] (Shapiro).
Run the proof of Lemma 15.13 with G′_∞ in place of G_∞.
Classification of the contained case: the quadratic subfields of Q(μ_{p^∞}) are Q(√(p*)) for p odd (p* = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p), imaginary exactly when p ≡ 3 mod 4, and Q(i), Q(√2), Q(√−2) for p = 2.
acceptance: K = Q(i), p = 2: contained case; K = Q(√−3), p = 3: contained case; K = Q(√−7), p = 7: contained case; K = Q(i), p = 5: not contained.
Burungale–Tian footnote 4 overlooks this case (PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/E13); Kato's own 15.15 and 15.17 use 15.14 there.
