Theorem 1.2 follows from Smith's distribution theorem and the 2-converse Theorem 1.1 for the congruent-number curve, which has CM by Q(i); so it rests on the case K = Q(i), p = 2.
Kato states only the case K ⊂ Q(ζ_{p^∞}); the list of such K (quadratic subfields of cyclotomic p-power fields) is an elementary addition made here.

nodes.title: Kato's length lemma (Lemma 14.15)
nodes.statement: Let A be a noetherian commutative ring, C the category of finitely generated A-modules with support of codimension ≥ 2, G(C) its Grothendieck group, M a finitely generated A-module with support of codimension ≥ 1, and a ∈ A such that M_𝔮 = 0 for every height-one prime 𝔮 containing a. Then M/aM and M[a] = Ker(a: M → M) lie in C, and [M/aM] − [M[a]] = Σ_𝔮 length_{A_𝔮}(M_𝔮)·[A/(𝔮 + aA)] in G(C), the sum over height-one primes 𝔮 not containing a.
hypotheses: A noetherian; M supported in codimension ≥ 1; M_𝔮 = 0 at height-one primes containing a.
proofSteps: Filter M with graded pieces either in C or isomorphic to A/𝔮 with 𝔮 of height one not containing a (prime filtration).
Both sides are additive in short exact sequences (the snake lemma for multiplication by a).
For pieces in C both sides vanish in G(C) after the correction; for A/𝔮 the left side is [A/(𝔮 + aA)] and A/𝔮 has no a-torsion.
acceptance: Applied to M₁ = H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q and M₂ = H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q/A·z in the proof of Prop. 15.17 and in equality-descent; Kato's proof of 15.17 misprints the reference as 'Lemma 14.12' (CMAllPrimeMainConjectures/E1).

sources.match: The identity in the Grothendieck group of modules supported in codimension ≥ 2 relating M/aM, M[a] and the height-one lengths of M at primes not containing a.
Applies this lemma (printed as 'Lemma 14.12') to H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q and H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q/A·(z ⊗ T(−1)).

nodes.title: The CM case of Kato's Theorem 12.4: H² torsion and H¹ free of rank one
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized CM newform of weight k ≥ 2 attached to ψ of conductor f, p any prime, λ | p, Λ_Q = O_λ[[G_∞]][1/p]. Then H^2(V_{F_λ}(f)) is a torsion Λ_Q-module and H^1(V_{F_λ}(f)) is Λ_Q-free of rank one; for every stable lattice T, H^2(T) is torsion and H^1(T) torsion-free. The proof uses only elliptic units, Rubin's inequality and descent; it uses no Beilinson–Kato class and not (15.16.1).
hypotheses: Every prime p, including p = 2 with K = Q(i) (the §15.14 case) and p dividing #Δ_f.
This is the early export to KatoEulerSystems L4/rational-iwasawa-module-structure for CM forms and to CMRankZeroConverse.
proofSteps: Extend coefficients to L ⊃ F; since H^2(V_{F_λ}(f)) ⊗ O_v ≅ H^2(V~_{L_v}(ψ)), it suffices to treat V~(ψ) (cm-induction-normalization (15.11.2)).

Assume K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}). Let 𝔭 be a height-zero prime of O_λ[[G_∞]] and q its inverse image, a height-one prime with p ∉ q. The image of z_{p∞f} ⊗ V(ψ)(−1) under H^1_{p∞f} → H^1(V~(ψ))_𝔭 (cm-comparison-map) is nonzero: at a finite-order character χ in the component of 𝔭, its dual exponential has period sums L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ∘N, k − 1)·γ in S(ψ)-terms by cm-elliptic-reciprocity, and cm-twist-nonvanishing gives χ with this value nonzero. Kato phrases this step with (15.12.2); only its S(ψ)-valued form, which needs no archimedean normalization (15.11.3), is used here.
H^1_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q is free of rank one (twisted-tower-cohomology (b)), so it is generated by the image of z_{p∞f} ⊗ V(ψ)(−1).

Rubin's inequality at q, in the twisted form given by elliptic-unit-euler-system-bound (Johnson-Leung–Kings Corollary 6.5 after twisting by χ_T), gives length H^2_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q ≤ length of the quotient by the elliptic units = 0; so H^2_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q = 0 and by (15.13.1) H^2(V~(ψ))_𝔭 = 0.
Hence H^2 is torsion; H^1 is free of rank one by the argument of Kato 13.8 (Euler characteristic and torsion-freeness).
If K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}) use cm-contained-descent in place of Lemma 15.13.
acceptance: For f = 32.2.a.a and p = 2 (K = Q(i) ⊂ Q(μ_{2^∞})): H^2(V_{Q_2}(f)) is torsion over Z_2[[Z_2^×]][1/2] and H^1 is free of rank one.
Kato's Theorem 13.4 does not apply to CM forms because its hypothesis (v) (an element of Gal(Q̄/Q(ζ_{p^∞})) with one-dimensional fixed quotient) fails; this node is the replacement.

sources.match: Proves Theorem 12.4 for CM f: nonvanishing from 13.5 and (15.12.2), freeness of H^1_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q, Rubin's theorem 15.2 to kill H^2_{p∞f}(V(ψ))_q, then (15.13.1); the contained case by 15.14.
Theorem 13.4 is not applied for CM forms because condition (v) fails.
States Kato's Theorem 12.4 for every newform and every prime.

nodes.title: Kato's inequality for CM forms (Prop. 15.17)
nodes.statement: Let λ | p be a finite place of L, 𝔭 a height-one prime of O_λ[[G_∞]], and assume 𝔭 ∌ p, or (Rubin's condition (b)) p ∤ #μ(H) and p ∤ #(torsion of G_{p∞f}). For a stable lattice T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ) let Z(ψ, T)_𝔭 be the O_λ[[G_∞]]_𝔭-submodule of H^1(T~)_𝔭 generated by the image of z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) under (15.12.1). Then length(H^2(T~)_𝔭) ≤ length(H^1(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ, T)_𝔭).
hypotheses: K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}), or the §15.14 variant when K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}).
Only the inequality: Kato does not prove equality in §15 (PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/E2).
proofSteps: Let q be the inverse image of 𝔭 and A = O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q, regular with the kernel to the cyclotomic localization generated by a (cm-descent-lemma).
Apply grothendieck-length-lemma to M₁ = H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q and M₂ = H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q/A·(z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1)) (Kato misprints the reference as Lemma 14.12; CMAllPrimeMainConjectures/E1).

With (15.13.1)–(15.13.2), the lengths over the cyclotomic localization are computed from the height-one lengths of M₁ and M₂ over A; Rubin's inequality at those height-one primes (elliptic-unit-euler-system-bound, twisted) gives the result.
acceptance: This node is the CM-branch input for KatoEulerSystems L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction in the Z(ψ, T) form; its Z(f) form needs (15.16.1) (cm-zeta-bridge) and is cm-kato-divisibility.

nodes.title: Kato's archimedean normalization of the CM induction (Lemma 15.11(2))
nodes.statement: With (15.11.1) fixed, let V~_L(ψ) = V_L(ψ) ⊕ ιV_L(ψ) be the representation of Gal(C/R) over L induced from V_L(ψ), and write per_ψ also for S(ψ) → V_C(ψ) ⊂ V~_C(ψ). There is a unique Gal(C/R)-isomorphism (15.11.3) V~_L(ψ) ≅ V_L(f) such that per_f corresponds to per_ψ under (15.11.1). It serves only to transport elements γ ∈ V_L(ψ) to γ′ ∈ V_L(f): Kato does not know that it is compatible with (15.11.2) for k ≥ 3 (the motives of f and of ψ are not known to coincide) and never uses it as an identification of Galois modules.
hypotheses: (15.11.1) is fixed; f is a CM newform attached to ψ.
proofSteps: Fix a sign ±. By Kato 6.6 (the period computation for modular zeta elements, KatoEulerSystems L3/archimedean-period-quotient-and-critical-values), cm-twist-nonvanishing and (15.9.2) (cm-eisenstein-evaluation), choose m ≥ 1, z ∈ S(ψ) ⊗ Q(ζ_m), z′ ∈ S(f) ⊗ Q(ζ_m) and nonzero γ, γ′ such that the χ-twisted period sums of z and z′ are L_S(ψ̄, χ, k − 1)γ and L_S(f*, χ, k − 1)γ′ for every χ of sign ±, S = prime(mN), with some χ of sign ± having nonzero value; the two L-values agree since L(f*, s) = L(ψ̄, s). Kato writes ψ and f here (CMAllPrimeMainConjectures/E2); the argument is the same.

Let b ∈ L(ζ_m) be the ratio of the images of σ₀(z′) and σ₀(z) in S(ψ) ⊗ L(ζ_m) for a σ₀ making the image nonzero. Averaging over characters shows that the twisted sums determine b and that b is fixed by Gal(L(ζ_m)/L), so b ∈ L^×.
Define h on the ± part by γ ↦ b^{-1}γ′; then h ∘ per_ψ = per_f. Uniqueness is clear since both sides are one-dimensional on each sign.

nodes.title: The reciprocity law in V(f)-coefficients (15.12.2)
nodes.statement: Let γ ∈ V_L(ψ) and γ′ ∈ V_L(f) its image under (15.11.3). For n ≥ 0, the composite of the Tate-twisted map (15.12.1), H¹_{p∞f}(V(ψ)(1)) → H¹(V(f)(1)), with specialization at level n, localization at p and exp^*: H^1_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗ V_L(ψ) → S(f) ⊗_F L_λ ⊗ Q(ζ_{p^n}), extended to S^{-1}H^1_{p∞f} for S the non-zero-divisors invertible in Q_p[Gal(Q(ζ_{p^n})/Q)], sends z_{p∞f} ⊗ γ into S(f) ⊗_F L ⊗ Q(ζ_{p^n}), and for every χ: Gal(Q(ζ_{p^n})/Q) → C^×, Σ_σ χ(σ)·per_f(σ(image)) = L_{{p}}(f*, χ, k − 1)·(γ′)^±, with ± = χ(−1), where f* is the newform with complex-conjugate coefficients and L_{{p}} omits only the Euler factor at p.
hypotheses: r = k − 1, f ⊂ cond(ψ); every prime p.
(15.11.3) enters only through γ ↦ γ′.
The ideal f is exactly the conductor of ψ, not an arbitrary smaller ideal contained in it. A larger modulus leaves extra Euler factors and does not yield the stated L_{ {p} } value.
proofSteps: At level n use the compositum K·Q(ζ_{p^n}) inside K(p^∞f), or the corresponding finite étale algebra K ⊗_Q Q(ζ_{p^n}) when it splits. First map H¹(Z_p(1)) ⊗ V(ψ) into H¹(V(ψ)(1)), then apply (15.12.1) twisted by (1), corestriction/Shapiro, localization and the dual exponential. This is the typed composite in Kato (15.12.2), p. 263.
Translate S(ψ)-valued periods into S(f)-valued ones with (15.11.1) and per_ψ into per_f with (15.11.3); the sign component of γ′ is selected by χ(−1).

Compare L-values: for χ a character of Gal(Q(ζ_{p^n})/Q), L_{pf}(ψ̄, χ∘N_{K/Q}, k − 1) = L_{{p}}(f*, χ, k − 1), since L(f*, s) = L(ψ̄, s) and the Euler factors of f* at the primes of f (the conductor of ψ, where ψ̄ is ramified) are trivial.
acceptance: The value has the same shape as Kato's Theorem 12.5(1) for the Beilinson–Kato elements, (2πi)^{k−r−1}L_{{p}}(f*, χ, r)γ^± at r = k − 1, which is what cm-zeta-bridge compares.

nodes.title: The equivariant equality on ψ-components with lattice coefficients
nodes.statement: Let ψ have conductor f, T ⊂ V_{L_λ}(ψ) a stable lattice, A = O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]. For every height-one prime q′ of A with p ∉ q′ that is contained in the inverse image q of a prime 𝔭 ∌ p of O_λ[[G_∞]] (of O_λ[[G′_∞]] when K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞})): length(H^2_{p∞f}(T)_{q′}) = length((H^1_{p∞f}(T)/A·(z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1)))_{q′}).
hypotheses: f is the conductor of ψ, so every 𝔩 | f with 𝔩 ∤ p is ramified for ψ.
Rational statement: only primes not containing p.
proofSteps: Twist by twisted-tower-cohomology (a): H^q_{p∞f}(T)_{q′} ≅ (H^q_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)) ⊗ O_λ)_{Tw_{χ_T}(q′)}, carrying the elliptic-unit span to z ⊗ O_λ.

Apply rational-equivariant-main-conjecture over O_λ (flat base change) at the regular prime Tw_{χ_T}(q′): lengths of H^2_{pf} and of h¹/z agree, and h² differs from H^2_{pf} by the Euler terms Z_p[[G/D_𝔩]].

Kill the Euler terms. Let g ∈ I_𝔩; it has finite order and maps to 1 in G_∞, so g − 1 lies in the kernel of the restriction map and hence in q. A height-one q′ ⊂ q contains g − ζ for some root of unity ζ (because g^m − 1 = 0), and then ζ − 1 ∈ q; as p ∉ q this forces ζ = 1, so g − 1 ∈ q′. After the twist the Euler module O_λ[[G/D_𝔩]] is killed by χ_T(g)^{-1}g − 1, which is congruent to χ_T(g)^{-1} − 1 modulo q′. That is nonzero in the residue field, of characteristic zero, because χ_T|_{I_𝔩} = ψ|_{I_𝔩} ≠ 1 (𝔩 divides the conductor of ψ). So the localized Euler term vanishes (h2-euler-comparison).
Combine with class-module-h2-comparison to replace h² by H^2_{p∞f}(Z_p(1)).
acceptance: When every prime of f lies above p there are no Euler terms to kill.

nodes.title: Elliptic units specialize to Beilinson–Kato elements (Kato (15.16.1))
nodes.statement: Let f be a CM newform attached to ψ, enlarge coefficients to L ⊃ F containing the values of ψ, and let γ ∈ V_L(ψ) with image γ′ ∈ V_L(f) under (15.11.3). Then (15.12.1) sends z_{p∞f} ⊗ γ ⊗ (ζ_{p^n})_n^{⊗(−1)} to z^{(p)}_{γ′} = z_{γ′}(f), the value at γ′ of Kato's zeta map V_{F_λ}(f) → H^1(V_{F_λ}(f)) (KatoEulerSystems L2/rational-kato-zeta-morphism), extended L-linearly. Consequently the Λ_Q-span of the images of z_{p∞f} ⊗ V_L(ψ)(−1) is Z(f) ⊗ L.
hypotheses: Kato's zeta map for CM forms is constructed using the CM case of Theorem 12.4(2), supplied by cm-h2-torsion; no circularity, since cm-h2-torsion uses only (15.12.2).
K ⊄ Q(μ_{p^∞}) in Kato's text; for K ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}) (K = Q(i), p = 2) the same deduction applies, since 13.9–13.13 use only 12.4 and 13.5–13.6.
proofSteps: Both sides lie in H^1(V(f)), which is free of rank one over Λ_Q (cm-h2-torsion).

Their dual-exponential images at every finite level and every finite-order character agree: for the elliptic side by cm-coefficient-reciprocity, for the Kato side by KatoEulerSystems L3/zeta-class-interpolation-of-complex-L-values (Kato Theorem 12.5(1)), both equal to L_{{p}}(f*, χ, k − 1)(γ′)^± (times the same archimedean factor) with the same periods because (15.11.1) and (15.11.3) were fixed compatibly.

Use nonvanishing from cm-twist-nonvanishing and the finite-level exponential rank calculation in Kato §§13.9–13.13 on each cyclotomic component. At infinitely many finite-order characters where the displayed L-value is nonzero, the dual exponential is injective on the relevant specialized rank-one line. Their difference therefore specializes to zero at a dense set; the power-series uniqueness argument kills the difference in the free rank-one Λ_Q-module. Equality of exponential images alone would not give injectivity without these inputs.
Integrality is not asserted.
acceptance: For f = 32.2.a.a and p = 2 this identifies the elliptic units of the 2-power ray tower of Q(i) with the Beilinson–Kato element of the congruent-number curve, after the §15.14 base change.

The link between Beilinson–Kato elements and elliptic units, Kato (15.16.1), is the basis of the proof.

nodes.title: From the equivariant equality to Kato's equality at cyclotomic primes
nodes.statement: In the setting of cm-descent-lemma (or cm-contained-descent), with 𝔭 ∌ p, q its inverse image, A = O_λ[[G_{p∞f}]]_q regular with kernel generated by a prime element a, put M₁ = H^2_{p∞f}(T)_q and M₂ = H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q/A·(z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1)). If length(M₁)_{q′} = length(M₂)_{q′} at every height-one prime q′ of A, then length(H^2(T~)_𝔭) = length(H^1(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ, T)_𝔭).
hypotheses: A is a regular local ring, hence a unique factorization domain; a is a prime element.
H^1_{p∞f}(T)_q is torsion-free of rank one and z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) generates it at aA (from cm-h2-torsion's argument, Kato 15.15).
proofSteps: The only height-one prime of A containing a is aA, the inverse image of the generic point of the cyclotomic component; M₁ and M₂ vanish there (H² vanishes and z generates H¹ at aA, by the argument of cm-h2-torsion), so Lemma 14.15 applies. Since A is two-dimensional local, classes of modules supported in codimension two are lengths. Apply grothendieck-length-lemma to M₁ and M₂ with the element a: [M_i/aM_i] − [M_i[a]] = Σ_{q′ ∌ a} length(M_i)_{q′}[A/(q′ + aA)], so the hypothesis gives [M₁/aM₁] − [M₁[a]] = [M₂/aM₂] − [M₂[a]].
By (15.13.1), M₁/aM₁ = H^2(T~)_𝔭; by (15.13.2), H^1(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ,T)_𝔭 is an extension of M₁[a] by M₂/aM₂.

M₂[a] = 0: use the zeta generator to embed the torsion-free rank-one H¹ module as A ⊂ H ⊂ Frac(A), with H_(a) = A_(a). If ah ∈ A for h ∈ H, then h ∈ a^{-1}A ∩ A_(a) = A because A is a UFD and a is prime. Thus the class of h in H/A is zero.
Hence length(H^2(T~)_𝔭) = length(M₁/aM₁) = length(M₂/aM₂) + length(M₁[a]) = length(H^1(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ,T)_𝔭): the Ker(a | M₁) terms cancel.
The integrality of z_{p∞f} ⊗ T(−1) at q, implicit in Kato's proof, follows from (15.6.3) since N(a) − σ_a is a unit at q for a suitable auxiliary a.
acceptance: This is the step Burungale–Tian attribute to Kato §15, which proves only the inequality (PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/E2).

nodes.title: Kato's main conjecture for every CM newform and every prime (Burungale–Tian Theorem 2.6)

Then ξ(H^2(V)) = ξ(H^1(V)/Z(f)) as ideals of Λ_Q = O_λ[[G_∞]][1/p].

p = 2 and K = Q(i) included (§15.14); p dividing #Δ included, since only primes not containing p matter after inverting p.

By cm-zeta-bridge, Z(f) ⊗ L is the span of the images of z_{p∞f} ⊗ V(ψ)(−1), i.e. Z(ψ, T) ⊗ Q for any lattice T.

For each height-one prime 𝔭 ∌ p of O_λ[[G_∞]]: twisted-equivariant-equality supplies the hypothesis of equality-descent, which gives length(H^2(T~)_𝔭) = length(H^1(T~)_𝔭/Z(ψ,T)_𝔭); use cm-descent-lemma or cm-contained-descent according as K ⊄ or ⊂ Q(μ_{p^∞}).
H^2(V) is torsion and H^1(V) free of rank one (cm-h2-torsion), so both characteristic ideals are defined, and equal lengths at every height-one prime of Λ_Q give equal ideals.
